body.text: Harṣadeva: Ratnāvalīnāṭikā
(Act I)

pādāgrasthitayā muhuḥ stanabhareṇānītayā namratāṃ
śaṃbhoḥ saspṛhalocanatrayapathaṃ yāntyā tadārādhane |
hrīmatyā śirasīhitaḥ sapulakasvedodgamotkampayā
viśliṣyan kusumāñjalir girijayā kṣipto 'ntare pātu vaḥ || 1 || (1.1)
api ca |
autsukyena kṛtatvarā sahabhuvā vyāvartamānā hriyā
tais tair bandhuvadhūjanasya vacanair nītābhimukhyaṃ punaḥ |
dṛṣṭvāgre varam āttasādhvasarasā gaurī nave saṃgame
saṃrohatpulakā hareṇa hasatā śliṣṭā śivāyāstu vaḥ || 2 || (1.2)
api ca |
krodheddhair dṛṣtipātais tribhir upaśamitā vahnayo 'mī trayo 'pi
trāsārtā ṛtvijo 'dhaś capalagaṇahṛtoṣṇīṣapaṭṭāḥ patanti |
dakṣaḥ stautyasya patnī vilapati kṛpaṇaṃ vidrutaṃ cāpi devaiḥ
śaṃsan nityāttahāso makhamathanavidhau pātu devyai śivo vaḥ || 3 || (1.3)
api ca |
jitam uḍupatinā namaḥ surebhyo
dvijavṛṣabhā nirupadravā bhavantu |
bhavatu ca pṛthivī samṛddhasasyā
pratapatu candravapur narendracandraḥ || 4 || (1.4)

(1.1) nāndyante
Sūtradhāraḥ | alam ativistareṇa | adyāhaṃ vasantotsave sabahumānam āhūya nānādigdeśāgatena rājñaḥ śrīharṣadevasya pādapadmopajīvinā rājasamūhenokto yathā | asmatsvāminā śrīharṣadevenāpūrvavasturacanālaṅkṛtā ratnāvalī nāma nāṭikā kṛtety asmābhiḥ śrotraparamparayā śrutā na tu prayogato dṛṣṭā | tat tasyaiva rājñaḥ sakalajanahṛdayāhlādino bahumānād asmāsu cānugrahabuddhyā yathāvat prayogeṇa tvayā nāṭayitavyeti | tad yāvad idānīṃ nepathyaracanāṃ kṛtvā yathābhilaṣitaṃ saṃpādayāmi | parikramyāvalokya ca | aye | āvarjitāni sakalasāmājikānāṃ manāṃsīti me niścayaḥ | kutaḥ |
śrīharṣo nipuṇaḥ kaviḥ pariṣad apy eṣā guṇagrāhiṇī
loke hāri ca vatsarājacaritaṃ nāṭye ca dakṣā vayaṃ |
vastv ekaikam apīha vāñchitaphalaprāpteḥ padaṃ kiṃ punar
madbhāgyopacayād ayaṃ samuditaḥ sarvo guṇānāṃ gaṇaḥ || 5 || (1.5)
tad yāvad ahaṃ gṛhaṃ gatvā gṛhiṇīm āhūya saṃgītakam anutiṣṭhāmi | parikramya nepathyābhimukham avalokya ca | idam asmadīyaṃ gṛham | yāvat praviśāmi | uccaiḥ | ārye | itas tāvat |
(1.2) praviśya
Naṭī | ajjautta | iamhi | āṇavedu ajjo | ko ṇioo aṇuciṭṭhīadu tti |
(1.3) Sūtradhāraḥ | ārye | ratnāvalīdarśanotsuko 'yaṃ rājalokaḥ | tad gṛhyatāṃ nepathyam |
(1.4) Naṭī | sodvegam | ajja | ṇiccinto dāṇiṃ si tumaṃ | tā kīsa ṇa ṇaccasi | mama uṇa mandabhāiṇīe ekkā jjevva duhidā | sā vi tae kahiṃ pi desantare diṇṇā | dūraṭṭhideṇa jāmāduṇā se pāṇiggahaṇaṃ kadhaṃ bhavissadi tti imāe cintāe appā vi ṇa me paḍibhādi | kiṃ uṇa ṇaccidavvaṃ |
(1.5) Sūtradhāraḥ | ārye | dūrasthitenety alam udvegena | paśya |
dvīpād anyasmād api madhyād api jalanidher diśo 'py antāt |
ānīya jhaṭiti ghaṭayati vidhir abhimatam abhimukhībhūtaḥ || 6 || (1.6)
(1.6) Nepathye | sādhu bharataputra sādhu | evam etat | kaḥ saṃdehaḥ | dvīpād anyasmād iti punaḥ paṭhati |
(1.7) Sūtradhāraḥ | ākarṇya nepathyābhimukham avalokya ca | ārye | kim ataḥ paraṃ vilambase | nanv ayaṃ mama kanīyān bhrātā gṛhītayaugandharāyaṇabhūmikaḥ prāpta eva | tad ehi | nepathyagrahaṇāya sajjībhavāva | iti niṣkrāntau |
iti prastāvanā |

tataḥ praviśati yaugandharāyaṇaḥ |
(1.8) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | evam etat | kaḥ saṃdehaḥ | dvīpād anyasmād iti punaḥ paṭhati | anyathā kva siddhādeśapratyayaprārthitāyāḥ siṃhaleśvaraduhituḥ samudre pravahaṇabhaṅganimagnāyāḥ phalakāsādanaṃ kva ca kauśāmbīyena vaṇijā siṃhalebhyaḥ pratyāgacchatā tadavasthāyāḥ saṃbhāvanaṃ ratnamālācihnāyāś cehānayanam | sarvathā spṛśanti naḥ svāminam abhyudayāḥ | vicintya | mayāpi caināṃ devīhaste sagauravaṃ nikṣipatā yuktam evānuṣṭhitam | śrutaṃ ca mayā | bābhravyo 'pi kañcukī vasubhūtinā siṃhaleśvarāmātyena saha kathaṃ katham api samudrād uttīrya kosalocchittaye gatasya rumaṇvato milita iti | tad evaṃ niṣpannaprāyam api prayojanaṃ na me dhṛtim āvahati | kaṣṭo 'yaṃ khalu bhṛtyabhāvaḥ | kutaḥ |
prārambhe 'smin svāmino vṛddhihetau
daivenetthaṃ dattahastāvalambe |
siddher bhrāntir nāsti satyaṃ tathāpi
svecchācārī bhīta evāsmi bhartuḥ || 7 || (1.7)
nepathye kalakalaḥ |
(1.9) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | ākarṇya | aye | yathāyam abhihanyamānamṛdumṛdaṅgānugatasaṃgītamadhuraḥ puraḥ paurāṇām uccarati carcarīdhvanis tathā tarkayāmi | madanamahamahīyāṃsaṃ purajanapramodam avalokayituṃ prāsādābhimukhaṃ prasthito deva iti | ūrdhvam avalokya | aye katham | adhirūḍha eva devaḥ prāsādaṃ | ya eṣa
viśrāntavigrahakatho ratimāñ janasya
citte vasan priyavasantaka eva sākṣāt |
paryutsuko nijamahotsavadarśanāya
vatseśvaraḥ kusumacāpa ivābhyupaiti || 8 || (1.8)
tad yāvad gṛhaṃ gatvā kāryaśeṣaṃ cintayāmi | iti niṣkrāntaḥ |
iti viṣkambhakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> enters. (1.8) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: It is so. What doubt is there? (He reads again: 'from another island.') Otherwise, how [to explain] the finding on a plank of the daughter of the king of <s>Siṃhala</s>, who was sought because of faith in the prophecy of a <s>siddha</s> (perfected ascetic), and who was submerged in the ocean due to a shipwreck; and how [to explain] the recognition of her condition and the bringing here of the woman bearing the jewel-necklace as identification, by a merchant of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> returning from <s>Siṃhala</s>? In every way, good fortunes touch our master. (Reflecting) And I too have acted rightly in respectfully placing her in the queen's hands. And I have heard that the chamberlain <s>Bābhravya</s> too, having somehow crossed the ocean together with <s>Vasubhūti</s>, the minister of the king of <s>Siṃhala</s>, has met <s>Rumaṇvat</s> who had gone to destroy <s>Kosala</s>. Even though the purpose is nearly accomplished, it does not bring me confidence. Hard indeed is this state of being a servant! Why? [Verse 7:] In this undertaking aimed at my master's prosperity, / with destiny thus extending a helping hand, / there is truly no doubt about success; yet, / being one who acts at his own discretion, I am fearful of my lord. (Noise offstage.) (1.9) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: (Listening) Oh! By the way this sound of <s>carcarī</s> song rises before the citizens, sweet with music accompanied by softly-struck <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums, I conclude that the king has set out toward the palace terrace to observe the great joy of the citizens during the <s>Madana</s> festival. (Looking up) Oh, what! The king has already ascended the palace! [Verse 8:] He whose tales of war have ceased, who delights in love, / dwelling in the hearts of the people — the dear Spring personified — / eager to behold his own great festival, / the lord of <s>Vatsa</s> approaches like <s>Kusumacāpa</s> (the Flower-Bowed One, <s>Kāmadeva</s>) himself. Then let me go home and consider the remaining business. (Exit.) Thus ends the <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (prologue).

tataḥ praviśaty āsanastho gṛhītavasantotsavaveṣo rājā vasantakaś ca |
(1.10) Rājā | sādaram | sakhe vasantaka |
(1.11) Vidūṣakaḥ | āṇavedu bhavaṃ |
(1.12) Rājā |
rājyaṃ nirjitaśatru yogyasacive nyastaḥ samasto bharaḥ
samyakpālanalālitāḥ praśamitāśeṣopasargāḥ prajāḥ |
pradyotasya sutā vasantasamayas tvaṃ ceti nāmnā dhṛtiṃ
kāmaḥ kāmam upaitv ayaṃ mama punar manye mahān utsavaḥ || 9 || (1.9)
(1.13) Vidūṣakaḥ | saharṣam | bho vaassa | evvaṃ ṇedaṃ | ahaṃ uṇa jāṇāmi | ṇa bhavado ṇa kāmadevassa mama jjevva ekkassa bamhaṇassa aaṃ maaṇamahūsavo tti jeṇa piavaasseṇa tumaṃ ti mantīadi | vilokya | tā kiṃ imiṇā | pekkha dāva imassa mahumattakāmiṇījaṇasaaṅgāhagahidaṇaccantaṇāarajaṇajaṇidakodūhalassa samantado saṃvuttamaddaluddāmacaccarīsaddamuhararacchāmuhasohiṇo paiṇṇapaḍavāsapuñjapiñjarijjantadahadisāmuhassa sasirīattaṇaṃ maaṇamahūsavassa |
(1.14) Rājā | saharṣaṃ samantād avalokya | aho | parāṃ koṭim adhirohati pramodaḥ puraḥ paurānām | tathā hi |
kīrṇaiḥ piṣṭātakaughaiḥ kṛtadivasamukhaiḥ kuṅkumakṣodagaurair
hemālaṅkārabhābhir bharanamitaśikhaiḥ śekharaiḥ kaiṅkirātaiḥ |
eṣā veṣābhilakṣyasvavibhavavijitāśeṣavitteśakośā
kauśāmbī śātakumbhadravakhacitajanevaikapītā vibhāti || 10 || (1.10)
api ca |dhārāyantravimuktasaṃtatapayaḥpūraplute sarvataḥ
sadyaḥ sāndravimardakardamakṛtakrīḍe kṣaṇam prāṅgaṇe |
uddāmapramadākapolanipatatsindūrarāgāruṇaiḥ
saindūrīkriyate janena caraṇanyāsaiḥ puraḥ kuṭṭimam || 11 || (1.11)
(1.15) Vidūṣakaḥ | vilokya | edaṃ pi dāva suviaḍḍhajaṇāpūridasiṅgaajalapahāramukkasikkāramaṇoharaṃ vāravilāsiṇījaṇavilasidaṃ avaloedu piavaasso |
(1.16) Rājā | vilokya | vayasya | samyag dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā | kutaḥ |

children.translated_text: In this darkness created by scattered strips of cloth,
barely visible through the net of rays from jeweled ornaments,
this serpent-world, with raised hoods appearing like peaks,
today reminds me of the subterranean realm. || 12 ||

body.translated_text:
Then enters the King, seated, wearing the attire of the spring festival, along with <s>Vasantaka</s>.
(1.10) King (with affection): Friend <s>Vasantaka</s>!
(1.11) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: May the lord command.
(1.12) King:
The kingdom's foes are conquered, the entire burden is entrusted to a capable minister,
the subjects are well-governed and nurtured, all calamities removed.
<s>Pradyota's</s> daughter, the spring season, and you — by name, satisfaction:
may <s>Kāma</s> (desire) indeed attain his fill, but I think this is a great festival for me. || 9 || (1.9)
(1.13) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (with delight): Dear friend! It is just so. But I know — not for you, not for the God of Love, but for me alone, a single <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is this the festival of the God of Love, since my dear friend addresses you so with affection. (Looking around) But what of this? Just behold the splendor of this festival of the God of Love, with its people captivated by the dances of women intoxicated with spring-wine, echoing on all sides with the resonant sounds of drums and cymbals!
(1.14) King (looking around with delight): Ah! The joy of the townspeople rises to its highest peak. For:
With heaps of scattered colored powders making the face of day bright, golden with saffron dust,
with festival garlands heavy with golden ornaments on bowed heads adorned with <s>kiṅkirāta</s> flowers,
this <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, whose own splendor visible in attire surpasses the entire treasury of the Lord of Wealth,
shines as if made entirely golden by the liquid of <s>Śātakumbha</s> gold applied to the people. || 10 || (1.10)
Moreover:
In the courtyards flooded everywhere with continuous streams of water released from fountain-machines,
instantly turned into a muddy playground from vigorous rubbing,
the people make the pavement of the street before them ruddy-red
with their footsteps reddened by the vermillion falling from the cheeks of exuberant women. || 11 || (1.11)
(1.15) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking): Let my dear friend also behold this charming sight — the play of courtesans, sprinkled with water from fountain-pipes filled by well-bred folk, delightful with their splashing sounds.
(1.16) King (looking): Friend, you have seen rightly. For —

body.text: (1.17) Vidūṣakaḥ | vilokya | bho vaassa | pekkha pekkha | esā khu maaṇiā maaṇasarisaṃ vasantāhiṇaaṃ ṇaccantī cūdaladiāe saha ido jjevva āacchadi |
body.translated_text: (1.17) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking): Dear friend! Look, look! Here comes <s>Madanikā</s>, dancing a dance befitting the spring festival, together with <s>Cūḍālatikā</s>, approaching right toward us.

children.text: tataḥ praviśato madalīlāṃ nāṭayantyau dvipadīkhaṇḍaṃ gāyantyau cetyau |
children.translated_text: Then the two enter, performing a dance of amorous grace, singing a two-line song.
(1.18) <s>Madanikā</s> sings:
The southern breeze blows, raising dust from flower-clusters,
with many fresh sprouts as garlands, loosening one's grip. || 13 ||
With sorrow increased by separation, longing for union with the beloved,
unable to endure the waiting — it is the companion of young women. || 14 ||

children.text: iha paḍhamaṃ mahumāso jaṇassa hiaāi kuṇai mauāiṃ |
children.translated_text: Here first the month of <s>Madhu</s> (spring) makes the hearts of people intoxicated,
afterwards <s>Kāma</s> (Love) strikes, with flower-arrows having found their opportunity. || 15 ||

body.text: (1.19) Rājā | nirvarṇya | aho madhuro 'yam āsāṃ nirbharaḥ krīḍārasaḥ |

children.text: srastaḥ sragdāmaśobhāṃ tyajati viracitām ākulaḥ keśapāśaḥ
children.translated_text: The garland-string, slipping down, abandons the arranged beauty of the disheveled hair;

children.text: kṣībāyā nūpurau ca dviguṇataram imau krandataḥ pādalagnau |
children.translated_text: the two anklets of the intoxicated one cry out with redoubled sound, clinging to her feet;

children.text: vyastaḥ kampānubandhād anavaratam uro hanti hāro 'yam asyāḥ
children.translated_text: this necklace, disordered from incessant trembling, strikes against her chest;
as she plays, heedless of the bending of her waist under the weight of her breasts, as if from the very strain. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: (1.19) King (gazing): Ah, how sweet is this overflowing playful sport of theirs!

body.text:
(1.20) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho vaassa | ahaṃ pi edāṇaṃ baddhapariarāṇaṃ majjhe ṇaccanto maaṇamahūsavaṃ māṇaissaṃ |
(1.21) Rājā | vayasya | evaṃ kriyatām |
(1.22) Vidūṣakaḥ | jaṃ bhavaṃ āṇavedi | ity utthāya ceṭyor madhye nṛtyati | bhodi maaṇie | mama vi edaṃ caccariṃ sikkhāvehi |
(1.23) Madanikā | ae hadāsa | ṇa esā caccarī |
(1.24) Vidūṣakaḥ | bhodi | kiṃ khu edaṃ |
(1.25) Madanikā | hadāsa | duvadīkhaṇḍaṃ kkhu edaṃ |
(1.26) Vidūṣakaḥ | saharṣam | kiṃ ediṇā khaṇḍeṇa modaā karīanti |
(1.27) Madanikā | vihasya | ṇa hi ṇa hi | paḍhīadi kkhu edaṃ |
(1.28) Vidūṣakaḥ | saviṣādam | jai paḍhīadi tā alaṃ ediṇā | varaṃ piavaassassa jjevva saāsaṃ gamissaṃ | iti gantum udyataḥ |
(1.29) Ubhe | haste gṛhītvā | hadāsa | kahiṃ gacchasi | idha jjevva kīlamha | iti ubhe vidūṣakaṃ bahuvidham ākarṣataḥ |
(1.30) Vidūṣakaḥ | hastam ākṛṣya prapalāyya rājānam upasṛtya | vaassa | ṇaccido mhi |
(1.31) Rājā | sādhu kṛtam |
(1.32) Cūtalatikā | halā maaṇie | ciraṃ khu amhehiṃ kīlidaṃ | tā ehi | ṇivedemha dāva bhaṭṭiṇīe saṃdesaṃ mahārāassa |
(1.33) Madanikā | ehi | tuvaramha | parikramyopasṛtya ca |
(1.34) Ubhe | jaadu jaadu bhaṭṭā | devī āṇavedi | ity ardhokte lajjāṃ nāṭayantyau | ṇa hi ṇa hi | viṇṇavedi |
(1.35) Rājā | saharṣaṃ vihasya sādaram | madanike | nanv ājñāpayatīty eva ramaṇīyaṃ viśeśato 'dya madanamahotsave | tad ucyatām | kim ājñāpayati devīti |
(1.36) Vidūṣakaḥ | ā dāsīe dhīe | kiṃ devī āṇavedi |
(1.37) Cetyau | evvaṃ bhaṭṭiṇī viṇṇavedi jadhā | ajja mae maarandujjāṇaṃ gadua rattāsoasaṃṭhidassa bhaavado kusumāuhassa pūā ṇivvattidavvā | tattha ajjautteṇa saṃṇihideṇa hodavvaṃ ti |
(1.38) Rājā | vayasya | kiṃ vyaktavyam | utsavād utsavāntaram āpatitam |
(1.39) Vidūṣakaḥ | tā uṭṭhehi | tahiṃ jevva gacchamha jeṇa tahiṃ gadassa mama vi bamhaṇassa sotthivāaṇaṃ kiṃ pi bhavissadi |
(1.40) Rājā | madanike | gamyatāṃ devyai nivedayituṃ | ayam aham āgata eva makarandodyānam iti |
(1.41) Ceṭyau | jaṃ bhaṭṭā āṇavedi | iti niṣkrānte |
(1.42) Rājā | vayasya | ehi | avatarāva |
ity utthāya prāsādāvataraṇaṃ nāṭayataḥ |
(1.43) Rājā | vayasya | ādeśaya makarandodyānasya mārgam |
(1.44) Vidūṣakaḥ | edu edu bhavaṃ |
iti parikrāmataḥ |
(1.45) Vidūṣakaḥ | agrato 'valokya | bho | edaṃ maarandujjāṇaṃ | tā ehi | pavisamha |
iti praviśataḥ |
(1.46) Vidūṣakaḥ | savismayam | bho mahārāa | pekkha pekkha | edaṃ taṃ malaamārudandolidamaulantasahaāramañjarīreṇupaḍalapaḍibaddhapaḍavidāṇaṃ mattamahuaraṇiaramukkajhaṅkāramilidamahuradarakoilālāvasaṃgīdasuhāvahaṃ tuha āgamaṇadaṃsidāaraṃ via maarandujjāṇaṃ lakkhīadi | tā avaloedu piavaasso |
(1.47) Rājā | samantād avalokya | aho ramyatā makarandodyānasya | iha hi
udyadvidrumakāntibhiḥ kisalayais tāmrāṃ tviṣaṃ bibhrato
bhṛṅgālīvirutaiḥ kalair aviśadavyāhāralīlābhṛtaḥ |
ghūrṇanto malayānilāhaticalaiḥ śākhāsamūhair muhur
bhrāntiṃ prāpya madhuprasaṅgam adhunā mattā ivāmī drumāḥ || 17 || (1.17)
api ca |mūle gaṇḍūṣasekāsava iva bakulair vamyate puṣpavṛṣtyā
madhvātāmre taruṇyā mukhaśaśini cirāc campakāny adya bhānti |
ākarṇyāśokapādāhatiṣu ca raṇatāṃ nirbharaṃ nūpurāṇāṃ
jhaṅkārasyānugītair anukaraṇam ivārabhyate bhṛṅgasārthaiḥ || 18 || (1.18)
(1.48) Vidūṣakaḥ | ākarṇya | bho vaassa | ṇa ede mahuarā ṇeurasaddaṃ aṇuharanti | ṇeurasaddo jjevva eso devīe pariaṇassa |
(1.49) Rājā | vayasya | samyag avadhāritam |
tataḥ praviśati vāsavadattā kāñcanamālā sāgarikā vibhavataś ca parīvārāḥ |
(1.50) Vāsavadattā | hañje kañcanamāle | ādesehi maarandujjāṇamaggaṃ |

(1.20) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Dear friend! I too shall now dance amidst the festive circle and honor the <s>Madana</s> festival like a lord!
(1.21) King: Friend, let it be done so!
(1.22) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: As the master commands! (Rising and dancing between the two maidservants) Lady <s>Madanikā</s>! Teach me this <s>carcarī</s> (dance-song) too!
(1.23) <s>Madanikā</s>: Oh fool! This is not a <s>carcarī</s>!
(1.24) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Lady! Then what is this?
(1.25) <s>Madanikā</s>: Fool! This is a <s>dvipadīkhaṇḍa</s> (a two-lined verse form)!
(1.26) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (With joy) Can sweets be made with this <s>khaṇḍa</s> (sugar)?
(1.27) <s>Madanikā</s>: (Laughing) No, no! It is recited!
(1.28) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (With dejection) If it is recited, then enough of this! Better that I go back to my dear friend! (He prepares to leave.)
(1.29) Both: (Seizing his hands) Fool! Where are you going? Let us play right here! (Both pull the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> in various ways.)
(1.30) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Pulling his hand away, fleeing, and approaching the king) Friend! I have been made to dance!
(1.31) King: Well done!
(1.32) <s>Cūtalatikā</s>: Dear <s>Madanikā</s>! We have played for a long time indeed! So come, let us first convey the queen's message to the great king.
(1.33) <s>Madanikā</s>: Come! Let us hurry! (They walk around and approach.)
(1.34) Both: Victory, victory to the lord! The queen commands — (Half-spoken, acting bashful) No, no! The queen humbly requests —
(1.35) King: (With joy, laughing, and with deference) <s>Madanikā</s>! Indeed 'commands' is itself charming, especially today at the <s>Madana</s> festival. So tell me — what does the queen command?
(1.36) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Oh, slave-girl's daughter! What does the queen command?
(1.37) The two maidservants: Thus the queen humbly requests: 'Today, having gone to the <s>Makaranda</s> garden, I must perform the worship of the blessed <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-Weaponed One, <s>Kāmadeva</s>), who is established at the red <s>Aśoka</s> tree. The noble lord should be present there.'
(1.38) King: Friend! What need be said? One festival has led into another!
(1.39) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Then arise! Let us go there, for having gone there, even for me, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, some benediction will surely be forthcoming!
(1.40) King: <s>Madanikā</s>! Go and inform the queen: 'I have already come to the <s>Makaranda</s> garden.'
(1.41) The two maidservants: As the lord commands! (They exit.)
(1.42) King: Friend! Come! Let us descend. (Rising, they act out descending from the palace.)
(1.43) King: Friend! Show the way to the <s>Makaranda</s> garden.
(1.44) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Let the master come, come! (They walk around.)
(1.45) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Looking ahead) Oh! This is the <s>Makaranda</s> garden! So come! Let us enter! (They enter.)
(1.46) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (With astonishment) Oh great king! Look, look! This <s>Makaranda</s> garden appears as if delighted by your arrival — with canopies formed by masses of pollen from clusters of blossoms at the tips swaying on branches stirred by the spring breeze, and with the sweet, soft cooing of cuckoos mingling with buzzing sounds released by intoxicated bees! So let the dear friend observe!
(1.47) King: (Looking all around) Oh, how lovely is the <s>Makaranda</s> garden! For here — [Verse 17:] With fresh shoots bearing a coppery luster through the rising coral-like beauty, / filled with the sweet unclear murmuring of rows of bees, / swaying again and again with their clusters of branches trembling from the blowing <s>Malaya</s> breeze, / these trees seem intoxicated, having become confused through the association with honey. // And moreover — [Verse 18:] Today the <s>bakula</s> trees seem to vomit a rain of flowers at their base like a gargling-libation of wine; / the <s>campaka</s> blossoms now shine as though on the moon-face of a young woman long suffused with the tawny hue of honey; / and upon hearing the anklets ring loudly when the <s>aśoka</s> trees are struck by [women's] feet, / swarms of bees seem to commence an imitation through their buzzing accompaniment. //
(1.48) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Listening) Oh friend! These are not bees imitating the sound of anklets! This is indeed the sound of anklets of the queen's retinue!
(1.49) King: Friend! Correctly observed. (Then enters <s>Vāsavadattā</s> with <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, <s>Sāgarikā</s>, and <s>Vibhavatas</s> as attendants.)
(1.50) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Dear <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! Show the way to the <s>Makaranda</s> garden.
(1.51) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: Let the queen come, come!
(1.52) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Walking around) Dear <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! How far now is that red <s>Aśoka</s> tree where I must perform the worship of the blessed <s>Madana</s>?
(1.53) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My queen! It is very near! Does the queen not see? This is indeed the <s>mādhavī</s> creeper, adopted by the queen, splendid with flowers blossoming without interruption. And this other is the <s>navamālikā</s> creeper, by whose abundance of freshly-blooming flowers the lord consoles himself. So passing beyond this, that very red <s>Aśoka</s> tree is visible where the queen will perform the worship.
(1.54) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Then come! Let us go there!
(1.55) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: Let the queen come, come! (All walk around.)
(1.56) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Here is that red <s>Aśoka</s> tree where I shall perform the worship. Therefore, bring me the offering materials for the worship.
(1.57) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: (Approaching) My queen! Everything is ready.
(1.58) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Examining, then aside) Oh, what negligence of the attendants! She who is being guarded from his sight has fallen within the very range of his gaze! But let it be so for now. (Aloud) Dear <s>Sāgarikā</s>! Why have you, while the attendants are occupied with the <s>Madana</s> festival, abandoned your <s>sārikā</s> (pet myna bird) and come here? So go back there quickly! And hand over all these worship materials to <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>!
(1.59) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: As the queen commands! (Doing so and walking a few steps, then aside) I have handed over the <s>sārikā</s> to a trustworthy friend's hands. Even so, I have a curiosity to see — is the blessed <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One, <s>Kāmadeva</s>) worshipped here in the same way as in the lord's inner chambers, or differently? So I shall watch unobserved. (Walking around and looking) While the worship-ceremony is taking place here, I too shall pick flowers to worship the blessed <s>Madana</s> himself! (She acts out picking flowers.)
(1.60) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! Install the image of the blessed <s>Pradyumna</s>!
(1.61) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: As the queen commands! (She does so.)
(1.62) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Walking around and looking) Oh friend! From the way the anklet-sound is spreading, I think the queen has come to the foot of the <s>Aśoka</s> tree!
(1.63) King: Friend! Correctly observed. Look! This —

body.translated_text: Then come, let us approach. [Approaching.] Dear <s>Vāsavadattā</s>! (1.64) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: [Looking.] What! My noble lord! Welcome, welcome, noble lord! Grace this place by accepting a seat. Here is a seat. Let the noble lord be seated here. [The King sits down in a theatrical manner.] (1.65) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady! The blessed lord <s>Pradyumna</s> [the god of love] has been honored — beautifully adorned with flowers, saffron, and sandalwood paste given by your own hand, and presented with an offering of red <s>aśoka</s> blossoms. (1.66) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Then bring me the articles for the prior worship. (1.67) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> brings them. (1.68) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> does accordingly. (1.69) The King: Dear <s>Vāsavadattā</s>! "With complexion clarified by the distinction of a fresh bath, beautiful with a garment glowing in the lovely redness of safflower, you shine as you worship the god of love — like a vine born from a young coral tree." || 20 || And further: "This <s>aśoka</s> tree, touched by your hand which is occupied in the worship of the god of love, O beloved, appears as though sprouting exceedingly tender new shoots." || 21 || And also: "This bodiless one [<s>Anaṅga</s>, the god of love] will today surely reproach his bodilessness, because he has not obtained the festival of the touch of your hand." || 22 || (1.70) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady! The blessed lord <s>Pradyumna</s> has been worshipped. Now perform the honor-offering for the noble lord. (1.71) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Then bring me flowers and unguent. (1.72) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady, everything is ready. (1.73) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> worships the King in a theatrical manner. (1.74) <s>Sāgarikā</s>, holding flowers: "Alas, alas! What! My heart, struck by the flower-arrow, has acted too hastily! But let me, screened by this <s>sindhuvāra</s> bush, watch from here." [Looking.] "What! Before my very eyes, the blessed god of flower-arrows is receiving worship! Then I too, standing right here, shall worship the blessed god of flower-arrows with these flowers." [She throws flowers.] "Homage to you, blessed god of flower-arrows! May you grant me an undeluded vision! I have seen what was to be seen." [She bows.] "How wonderful! Though seen, he is to be seen again! But let me depart before someone sees me." [She exits.] (1.75) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: Noble <s>Vasantaka</s>, come! Now accept the blessing gift. (1.76) The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> approaches. (1.77) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: [With the prior gift of unguent, flowers, and ornaments.] Noble <s>Vasantaka</s>, this is the blessing gift. [She presents it.] (1.78) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: [Receiving it joyfully.] Blessings to the lady! (1.79) Behind the curtain, the bard recites:

body.translated_text: Then <s>Susaṃgatā</s> enters, holding a cage with a <s>śārikā</s> (mynah bird) in her hand. (2.1) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Alas, alas! Where now has my dear friend <s>Sāgarikā</s> gone, having placed this mynah bird in my hands? (Looking elsewhere) Here comes <s>Nipuṇikā</s> this way. (Then <s>Nipuṇikā</s> enters.) (2.2) <s>Nipuṇikā</s>: I have learned my mistress's story. Let me go and report it to the queen. (She walks about.) (2.3) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend <s>Nipuṇikā</s>! Where are you going now, passing by me standing here as if with a mind struck by astonishment, disregarding me? (2.4) <s>Nipuṇikā</s>: What — <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Dear <s>Susaṃgatā</s>, you have guessed well! This indeed is the cause of my astonishment. Today, it seems, the master, having learned from the pious one named <s>Śrīkhaṇḍadāsa</s>, who has come from <s>Śrīparvata</s>, the longing for the sight of the <s>Aśoka</s> blossom, will beautify with the splendor of flowers the <s>Naumālikā</s> garden he has adopted as his own. I have been sent to report this matter to the queen. And where are you headed? (2.5) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: To seek my dear friend <s>Sāgarikā</s>. (2.6) <s>Nipuṇikā</s>: I saw <s>Sāgarikā</s> entering the painting hall, holding a box containing fruit as an offering for a picture. Go then to your dear friend! I too shall go to the queen's presence. (Both exit.) Thus ends the <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene).

(2.7) Sāgarikā | hiaa | pasīda pasīda | kiṃ imiṇā āāsamettaphalaeṇa dullahajaṇapatthaṇāṇubandheṇa | aṇṇaṃ ca | jeṇa jjevva diṭṭhametteṇa īdiso saṃtāvo vaṭṭadi puṇo vi taṃ jevva pekkhiduṃ ahilasasi tti aho de mūḍhadā | adiṇisaṃsa hiaa | jammado pahudi saha saṃvaḍḍhidaṃ imaṃ jaṇaṃ pariccaia khaṇamettadaṃsaṇaparicidaṃ jaṇaṃ aṇuacchanto ṇa lajjasi | adha vā ko tuha doso | aṇaṅgasarapaḍaṇabhīdeṇa tae evvaṃ ajjhavasidaṃ | bhodu | aṇaṅgaṃ dāva uvālahissaṃ | sāsram | bhaavaṃ kusumāuha | ṇijjidasurāsuro bhavia itthījaṇaṃ paharanto ṇa lajjasi | savvadhā mama mandabhāiṇīe imiṇā duṇṇimitteṇa avassaṃ maraṇaṃ uvaṭṭhidaṃ | phalakam avalokya | tā jāva ṇa ko vi idha āacchadi tāva ālekkhasamappidaṃ taṃ ahimadaṃ jaṇaṃ pekkhia jadhāsamīhidaṃ karissaṃ | sāvaṣṭambham ekamanā bhūtvā nāṭyena phalakaṃ gṛhītvā niḥśvas
ya | jai vi adisaddhaseṇa vevadi aaṃ adimettaṃ me aggahattho tadhā vi tassa jaṇassa aṇṇo daṃsaṇovāo ṇatthi tti jadhā tadhā ālihia pekkhissaṃ | iti nāṭyena likhati |
tataḥ praviśati susaṃgatā |
(2.8) Susaṃgatā | edaṃ khu kaalīharaṃ | tā jāva pavisāmi | praviśyāvalokya ca savismayaṃ | kiṃ uṇa esā garuāṇurāākhittahiaā ālihantī ṇa maṃ pekkhadi | tā jāva diṭṭhipadhaṃ se pariharia ṇirūvaissaṃ | svairaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'syāḥ sthitvā dṛṣṭvā ca saharṣam | kadhaṃ | bhaṭṭā ālihido | sāhu sāarie sāhu | adha vā ṇa kamalāaraṃ vajjia rāahaṃsī aṇṇassiṃ ahiramadi |
(2.9) Sāgarikā | sabāṣpam | ālihido mae eso | kiṃ uṇa ṇivaḍantabāhasalilā me diṭṭhī pekkhiduṃ ṇa pahavadi | ūrdhvam aśrūṇi saṃharantī susaṃgatāṃ dṛṣṭvottarīyeṇa pracchādayantī vilokya smitaṃ kṛtvā | kadhaṃ | susaṃgadā | sahi susaṃgade | ido uvavisa |
(2.10) Susaṃgatā | upaviśya phalakaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca | sahi | ko eso tae ālihido |
(2.11) Sāgarikā | sahi | ṇaṃ pauttamahūsavo bhaavaṃ aṇaṅgo |
(2.12) Susaṃgatā | savismayaṃ | aho de ṇiuṇattaṇaṃ | kiṃ uṇa suṇṇaṃ via cittaṃ paḍibhādi | tā ahaṃ pi ālihia radisaṇādhaṃ karissaṃ | vartikāṃ gṛhītvā nāṭyena likhati |
(2.13) Sāgarikā | vilokya sakrodham | sahi | kīsa tae ahaṃ ettha ālihidā |
(2.14) Susaṃgatā | sahi | kiṃ aāraṇe kuppasi | jādiso tae kāmadevo ālihido tādisī mae radī ālihidā | tā aṇṇadhāsaṃbhāviṇi kiṃ tuha ediṇā ālavideṇa | kadhehi savvaṃ vuttantaṃ |
(2.15) Sāgarikā | salajjā svagatam | ṇaṃ jāṇida mhi piasahīe | prakāśam | piasahi | mahadī khu me lajjā | tā tadhā karesu jadhā ṇa avaro ko vi edaṃ vuttantaṃ jāṇissadi |
(2.16) Susaṃgatā | sahi | mā lajja mā lajja | īdisassa kaṇṇaāraanassa avassaṃ jevva īdise vare ahilāseṇa hodavvaṃ | tadhā vi jadhā ṇa ko vi avaro edaṃ vuttantaṃ jāṇissadi tadhā karemi | edāe uṇa medhāviṇīe sāriāe ettha kāraṇeṇa hodavvaṃ | kadā vi esā imassa ālāvassa gahidakkharā kassa vi purado mantaissadi tti |
(2.17) Sāgarikā | sahi | ado vi me adhiadaraṃ saṃtāvo vaṭṭadi |
(2.18) Susaṃgatā | sāgarikāyā hṛdaye hastaṃ dattvā | sahi | samassasa samassasa | jāva imādo digghiādo ṇaliṇīvattaāiṃ muṇāliāo a geṇhia lahuṃ lahuṃ āacchāmi | niṣkramya punaḥ praviṣṭā nāṭyena nalinīpattrāṇi sāgarikāyā hṛdaye nikṣipati |
(2.19) Sāgarikā | sahi | avaṇehi imāiṃ ṇaliṇīvattāiṃ muṇāliāo a | alaṃ ediṇā | kīsa aāraṇe attāṇaaṃ āāsesi | ṇaṃ bhaṇāmi |
dullahajaṇāṇurāolajjā garuī paravvaso appā |
piasahi visamaṃ pemmaṃmaraṇaṃ saraṇaṃ ṇavaram ekkaṃ || 26 || (2.1)
iti mūrchati |
(2.20) Nepathye kalakalaḥ |
kaṇṭhe kṛttāvaśeṣaṃ kanakamayam adhaḥ śṛṅkhalādāma karṣan
krāntvā dvārāṇi helācalacaraṇaraṇatkiṅkiṇīcakravālaḥ |
dattātaṅko 'ṅganānām anusṛtasaraṇiḥ saṃbhramād aśvapālaiḥ
prabhraṣṭo 'yaṃ plavaṅgaḥ praviśati nṛpater mandiraṃ mandurāyāḥ || 27 || (2.2)
api ca |naṣṭaṃ varṣavarair manuṣyagaṇanābhāvād apāsya trapām
antaḥ kañcukikañcukasya viśati trāsād ayaṃ vāmanaḥ |
paryantāśrayibhir nijasya sadṛśaṃ nāmnaḥ kirātaiḥ kṛtaṃ
kubjā nīcatayaiva yānti śanakair ātmekṣaṇāśaṅkinaḥ || 28 || (2.3)
(2.21) Susaṃgatā | ākarṇya sasaṃbhramam | sahi | uṭṭhehi uṭṭhehi | eso kkhu duṭṭhavāṇaro ido jjevva āacchadi |
(2.22) Sāgarikā | kiṃ dāṇiṃ karissaṃ |
(2.23) Susaṃgatā | ehi | imassiṃ tamālaviḍavandhaāre pavisia edaṃ adivāhemha |
iti parikramyaikānte paryavasthite |
(2.24) Sāgarikā | susaṃgade | kadhaṃ | tae cittaphalao ujjhido | kadā vi ko vi taṃ pekkhissadi |
(2.25) Susaṃgatā | ai suṭṭhide | kiṃ ajja vi cittaphalaeṇa karissasi | eso vi dadhibhattalampaḍo edaṃ pañjaraṃ ugghāḍia duṭṭhavāṇaro adikkanto | esā khu medhāviṇī uḍḍīṇā aṇnado gacchadi | tā ehi | lahuṃ aṇusaramha |
(2.26) Sāgarikā | sahi | evvaṃ karemha |
iti parikrāmataḥ |
(2.27) Nepthye | hī hī bho | accharīaṃ accharīaṃ |
(2.28) Sāgarikā | sabhayaṃ vilokya | susaṃgade | jāṇīadi | puṇo vi duṭṭhavāṇaro jjevva āacchadi tti |
(2.29) Susaṃgatā | dṛṣṭvā vihasya | ai kādare | mā bhāāhi | bhaṭṭiṇo parivāsavattī khu eso ajja vasantao |
tataḥ praviśati vidūṣakaḥ |
(2.30) Vidūṣakaḥ | hī hī bho | accharīaṃ accharīaṃ | sāhu re sirikaṇḍadāsa dhammia sāhu |
(2.31) Sāgarikā saspṛham avalokayati |
(2.32) Susaṃgatā | sahi | kiṃ ediṇā diṭṭheṇa | dūrībhūdā khu sāriā | tā aṇusaramha |
iti niṣkrānte |
(2.33) Vidūṣakaḥ | sāhu re sirikaṇḍadāsa sāhu | jeṇa diṇṇametteṇa jjevva dohalaeṇa īdisī ṇomāliā saṃvuttā jeṇa ṇirantarubbhiṇṇakusumagucchacchādidaviḍavā uvahasantī via lakkhīadi devīparigahidaṃ māhavīladaṃ | tā jāva gadua piavaassassa ṇivedemi | parikramyāvalokya ca | eso kkhu piavaasso tassa dohalaassa laddhappaccaadāe parokkhaṃ pi taṃ ṇomāliaṃ paccakkhaṃ via kusumidaṃ pekkhanto harisupphullaloaṇo ido jjevva āacchadi | tā jāva ṇaṃ uvasappāmi | iti rājānaṃ prati gataḥ |
tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭo rājā |
(2.34) Rājā | saharṣaṃ |
uddāmotkalikāṃ vipāṇḍurarucaṃ prārabdhajṛmbhāṃ kṣaṇād
āyāsaṃ śvasanodgamair aviralair ātanvatīm ātmanaḥ |
adyodyānalatām imāṃ samadanāṃ nārīm ivānyāṃ dhruvaṃ
paśyan kopavipāṭaladyuti mukhaṃ devyāḥ kariṣyāmy aham || 29 || (2.4)
(2.35) Vidūṣakaḥ | sahasopasṛtya | jaadu jaadu piavaasso | bho vaassa | diṭṭhiā vaḍḍhasi | jeṇa diṇṇametteṇa iti puṇaḥ paṭhati |
(2.36) Rājā | kaḥ saṃdehaḥ | acintyo hi maṇimantrauṣadhīnāṃ prabhāvaḥ | tad ādeśaya mārgaṃ yena vayam api tadālokanena cakṣuṣaḥ phalam anubhavāmaḥ |
(2.37) Vidūṣakaḥ | sāṭopam | edu edu bhavaṃ |
ity ubhau parikrāmataḥ |
(2.38) Vidūṣakaḥ | ākarṇya sabhayaṃ nivṛtya rājānaṃ haste gṛhītvā sasaṃbhramam | bho vaassa | ehi | palāamha |
(2.39) Rājā | kim artham |
(2.40) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | edassiṃ baulapāave ko vi bhūdo paḍivasadi |
(2.41) Rājā | dhiṅ mūrkha | viśrabdhaṃ gamyatām | kuta īdṛśānām atra saṃbhavaḥ |
(2.42) Vidūṣakaḥ | phuḍakkharaṃ jevva mantedi | jai mama vaaṇaṃ ṇa pattiāasi tā aggado bhavia saaṃ jevva āaṇṇehi |
(2.43) Rājā | tathā kṛtvā śrutvā ca |
spaṣtākṣaram idaṃ tāvan madhuraṃ strīsvabhāvataḥ |
alpāṅgatvād anirhrādi manye vadati śārikā || 30 || (2.5)
ūrdhvaṃ nirūpya smitaṃ kṛtvā | śārikaiva |
(2.44) Vidūṣakaḥ | ūrdhvaṃ nirūpya | kadhaṃ | saccaṃ jevva sāriā |
(2.45) Rājā | vihasya | evam |
(2.46) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho vaassa | tumaṃ bhaāluo jeṇa sāriaṃ bhūdaṃ ti mantesi |
(2.47) Rājā | dhiṅ mūrkha | yad ātmanā kṛtam tan mayi saṃbhāvayasi |
(2.48) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | jai evvaṃ mā khu maṃ ṇivāresu | saroṣaṃ daṇḍakakāṣṭham udyamya | ā dāsīe dhīe sārie | tumaṃ jaṇāsi | saccaṃ jevva bamhaṇo bhaādi tti | tā ciṭṭha dāva | imiṇā pisuṇajaṇahiaakuḍileṇa daṇḍaaṭṭheṇa paripakkaṃ via phalaṃ imādo baulapāavādo tumaṃ pāḍaissaṃ | iti hantum udyataḥ |
(2.49) Rājā | nivārayan | kim apy eṣā ramaṇīyaṃ vyāharati | tat kiṃ enāṃ trāsayasi | śṛṇuvas tāvat |
ity ākarṇayataḥ |
(2.50) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | esā bhaṇādi | sahi | ko eso tae ālihido | sahi | ṇaṃ pauttamahūsavo bhaavaṃ aṇaṅgo tti | puṇo vi esā bhaṇādi | sahi | kīsa tae ahaṃ ettha ālihidā | sahi | kiṃ aāraṇe kuppasi | jādiso tae kāmadevo ālihido tādisī mae radī ālihidā | tā aṇṇadhāsaṃbhāviṇi | kiṃ tue ediṇā ālavideṇa | kadhehi savvaṃ vuttantaṃ ti | bho vaassa | kiṃ ṇedaṃ |
(2.51) Rājā | vayasya | evaṃ tarkayāmi | kayāpi hṛdayavallabho 'nurāgād ālikhya kāmadevavyapadeśena nihnutaḥ | tatsakhyāpi pratyabhijñāya vaidagdhyāt sāpi tatraiva rativyapadeśenālikhiteti |
(2.52) Vidūṣakaḥ | choṭikāṃ dattvā | jujjadi kkhu edaṃ |
(2.53) Rājā | vayasya | tūṣṇīṃ bhava | punar apy eṣā vyāharati |
(2.54) Vidūṣakaḥ | punar ākarṇya | bho | esā bhaṇādi | mā lajjā mā lajjā | īdisassa kaṇṇaāraaṇassa avassaṃ jevva īdise vare ahilāseṇa hodavvaṃ ti | bho vaassa | jā esā ālihidā sā khu kaṇṇaā daṃsaṇīā |
(2.55) Rājā | yady evam avahitau śṛṇuvas tāvat | asty avakāśo 'smākaṃ kautūhalasya |
(2.56) Vidūṣakaḥ | punar ākarṇya | bho | sudaṃ tae jaṃ edāe mantidaṃ | sahi | avaṇehi imāiṃ ṇaliṇīvattāiṃ muṇāliāo a | alaṃ ediṇā | kīsa aāraṇe attāṇaaṃ āāsesi tti |
(2.57) Rājā | vayasya | na kevala śrutam abhiprāyo 'pi lakṣita eva |
(2.58) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | mā paṇḍidagavvaṃ uvvaha | ahaṃ de savvaṃ suṇia vakkhāṇaissaṃ | suṇamha dāva | kiṃ kurukurāadi dāsīe dhīā sāriā |
(2.59) Rājā | yuktam abhihitam |
punar ākarṇayataḥ |
(2.60) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | esā dāsīe dhīā caduvvedī via bamhaṇo ricāiṃ paḍhiduṃ pauttā |
(2.61) Rājā | vayasya | kim apy anyacetasā mayā nāvadhāritam | tat kathaya | kim anyoktam |
(2.62) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | edaṃ edāe paḍhidaṃ | dullaha ityādi punaḥ paṭhati |
(2.63) Rājā | vihasya | sādhu mahābrāhmaṇa sādhu | ko 'nya evaṃvidhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhavantaṃ muktvaivaṃvidhānām ṛcām abhijñaḥ |
(2.64) Vidūṣakaḥ | kiṃ khu dāṇiṃ edaṃ |
(2.65) Rājā | mūrkha | gāthikeyam | kayāpi ślāghyayauvanayā priyatamam anāsādayantyā jīvitanirapekṣayoktam |
(2.66) Vidūṣakaḥ | uccair vihasya | ahaha | kiṃ edehiṃ vakkabhaṇidehiṃ | ujjuaṃ jevva kiṃ ṇa bhaṇāsi jadhā | maṃ aṇāsādaantīe tti | aṇṇadhā ko aṇṇo kusumacāvavavadeseṇa ṇiṇhūvīadi | uccair vihasya | ahaha |
(2.67) Rājā | ūrdhvam avalokya | dhiṅ mūrkha | kim uccair vihasatā tyayeyam uttrāsitā yenoḍḍīyāny atra kvāpi gatā |
(2.68) ubhau nirūpayataḥ |
(2.69) Vidūṣakaḥ | vilokya | bho esā khu kaalīhara gadā | tā lahuṃ aṇusaramha |
(2.70) Rājā | evaṃ bhavatu | parikramya |
durvārāṃ madanaśaravyathāṃ vahantyā
kāminyā yad abhihitaṃ puraḥ sakhīnām |
tad bhūyaḥ śiśuśukaśārikābhir uktaṃ
dhanyānāṃ śravaṇapathātithitvam eti || 31 || (2.5)
(2.71) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho vaassa | edaṃ kaalīharaṃ | jāva pavisamha |
ity ubhau praviśataḥ |
(2.72) Vidūṣakaḥ | kiṃ edāe dāsīe dhīāe sāriāe | idha dāva mandamāruduvvellidabālakaalīdalasīdale silādale uvavisia muhuttaaṃ vīsamha |
(2.73) Rājā | yad abhirucitaṃ bhavate |
ity upaviśataḥ |
(2.74) rājā durvārāmityādi punaḥ paṭhati |
(2.75) Vidūṣakaḥ | pārśvato 'valokya | ediṇā khu uṇa ugghāḍidaduvāreṇa tāe sāriāe pañjareṇa hodavvaṃ |
(2.76) Rājā | vayasya | nirūpyatām |
(2.77) Vidūṣakaḥ | jaṃ bhavaṃ āṇavedi | parikramyāvalokya ca | eso vi cittaphalao | jāva ṇaṃ geṇhāmi | phalakaṃ gṛhītvā nirūpya ca saharṣam | bho vaassa | diṭṭhiā vaḍḍhasi |
(2.78) Rājā | sakautukam | vayasya | kim etat |
(2.79) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | edaṃ khu taṃ jaṃ mae bhaṇidaṃ | tumaṃ jevva ettha ālihido | aṇṇadhā ko aṇṇo kusumacāvavavadeseṇa ṇiṇhūvīadi tti |
(2.80) Rājā | saharṣaṃ hastau prasārya | sakhe | upanaya |
(2.81) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | ṇa edaṃ daṃsaissaṃ | sā vi kaṇṇaā idha jjevva ālihidā ciṭṭhadi | tā kiṃ pāritosieṇa viṇā īdisaṃ kaṇṇaāraaṇaṃ daṃsīadi |
(2.82) Rājā | kaṭakaṃ samarpayann eva balād gṛhītvā savismayaṃ paśyati | vayasya |
līlāvadhūtapadmākathayantī pakṣapātam adhikaṃ naḥ |
mānasam upaiti keyañcitragatā rājahaṃsīva || 32 || (2.8)
api ca |vidhāyāpūrvapūrṇendum asyā mukham abhūd dhruvam |
dhātā nijāsanāmbhojavinimīlanaduḥsthitaḥ || 33 || (2.9)
tataḥ praviśati sāgarikā susaṃgatā ca |
(2.83) Susaṃgatā | sahi | ṇa samāsādidā sāriā | cittaphalaaṃ pi dāva imādo kaalīharādo geṇhia lahuṃ gacchamha |
(2.84) Sāgarikā | sahi | evvaṃ karemha |
ity upasarpataḥ |
(2.85) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | kīsa uṇa esā avaṇadamuhī ālihidā |
(2.86) Susaṃgatā | ākarṇya | sahi | jadhā vasantao mantedi tadhā takkemi | bhaṭṭiṇo vi idha jjevva hodavvaṃ ti | tā kaalīgummantaridāo bhavia pekkhamha |
ity ubhe ākarṇayataḥ |
(2.87) Rājā | vayasya | paśya paśya | vidhāyāpūrvapūrṇendum ityādi punaḥ paṭhati |
(2.88) Susaṃgatā | sahi | diṭṭhiā vaḍḍhasi | eso de piavallaho tumaṃ jevva ṇivvaṇṇaanto ciṭṭhadi |
(2.89) Sāgarikā | sahi | kiṃ ettha parihāsasīladāe imaṃ jaṇaṃ lahuṃ karesi |
(2.90) Vidūṣakaḥ | rājānaṃ cālayitvā | ṇaṃ bhaṇāmi | kīsa esā avaṇadamuhī ālihida tti |
(2.91) Rājā | vayasya | nanu śārikayaiva sarvam āveditam |
(2.92) Susaṃgatā | daṃsidaṃ khu medhāviṇīe attaṇo medhāvittaṇaṃ |
(2.93) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho | avi suhaadi de esā loaṇāiṃ ṇa vā |
(2.94) Sāgarikā | sasādhvasaṃ svagataṃ | kiṃ eso bhaṇissadi tti jaṃ saccaṃ maraṇajīvidāṇaṃ antare vaṭṭāmi |
(2.95) Rājā | vayasya | kim ucyate | mukhayatīti | paśya |
kṛccheṇoruyugaṃ vyatītya suciraṃ bhrāntvā nitambasyale
madhye 'syāstrīvalītaraṅgaviṣame niḥṣpandatām āgatā
me dṛṣṭis tṛṣiteva saṃprati śanair āruhya tuṅgau stanau
sākāṅkṣaṃ muhur īkṣate jalalavaprasyandinī locane || 34 || (2.9)
(2.96) Susaṃgatā | sahi | sudaṃ tae |
(2.97) Sāgarikā | sahi | tumaṃ jevva suṇa jāe ālekkhaviṇṇāṇaṃ vaṇṇīadi |
(2.98) Vidūṣakaḥ | bho vaassa | jassa uṇa īdisīo vi piasamāgamaṃ bahumaṇṇanti tassa de attaṇo uvari ko parihavo jeṇa imāe jjevva ālihidaṃ attāṇaaṃ ṇa pekkhasi |

Then enters <s>Sāgarikā</s>, holding a painting-board, acting out a state of lovesickness.
(2.7) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Heart! Be calm, be calm! What use is this painting-board that brings only the pursuit of an unattainable person? And moreover — by merely seeing him such burning agony arises, yet you long to see him again — oh, what foolishness of yours! Ungrateful heart! Abandoning this person with whom you have grown up together since birth, you are not ashamed to follow a person known only by a moment's glance! But then, what fault is yours? Struck by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One), you have thus resolved. So be it! First I shall reproach <s>Anaṅga</s>. (With tears) Lord <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-Weaponed One)! Having conquered both gods and demons, are you not ashamed to strike women? In every way, for me, an ill-fated woman, death has surely arrived because of this bad omen. (Looking at the board) So before anyone comes here, let me look at that beloved person entrusted to the painting and do as my heart desires. (With resolve, becoming single-minded, taking the board in dramatic gesture, sighing) Even though my body trembles with excessive timidity and my hand is most unsteady, still, since there is no other means of seeing that person, I shall draw him somehow and look. (She draws in dramatic gesture.)
Then enters <s>Susaṃgatā</s>.
(2.8) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: This is indeed the banana-grove. So let me enter. (Entering and looking with amazement) But what? She, with her heart seized by love for her mistress, is drawing and doesn't see me! So let me avoid the path of her gaze and observe. (Quietly standing behind her, looking with delight) What! The master has been drawn! Well done, <s>Sāgarikā</s>, well done! But then, does a royal swan delight in anything other than a lotus-pond?
(2.9) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (with tears): I have drawn him. But my eyes, flooding with streaming tears, are unable to see. (Wiping tears upward, seeing <s>Susaṃgatā</s>, covering [the board] with her upper garment, looking, smiling) What! <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Friend <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Come, sit here.
(2.10) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (sitting and looking at the board): Friend! Who is this drawn by you?
(2.11) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! It is the Lord <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless Love God) during his spring festival.
(2.12) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (with amazement): Oh, how skilled you are! But somehow the picture seems empty. So I too shall draw and complete it with <s>Rati</s>. (Taking a brush, she draws in dramatic gesture.)
(2.13) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (looking, with anger): Friend! Why have you drawn me here?
(2.14) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! Why are you angry without reason? Just as you drew the God of Love, so I drew <s>Rati</s>. So, you who pretend otherwise — what use is this evasion? Tell me the whole story.
(2.15) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (bashfully, aside): I have been found out by my dear friend! (Aloud) Dear friend! My shame is indeed great. So please act in such a way that no one else learns of this affair.
(2.16) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! Don't be ashamed, don't be ashamed! It is only natural that one of such ear-pleasing beauty should have desire for such a worthy match. Even so, I shall act so that no one else learns of this affair. But this clever mynah bird <s>Medhāvinī</s> should have nothing to do with this matter. She who has memorized the words of this conversation might repeat them before someone sometime.
(2.17) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! On that very account, my burning anguish increases even more.
(2.18) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (placing her hand on <s>Sāgarikā</s>'s heart): Friend! Be comforted, be comforted! While I quickly go and return, bringing lotus-leaves and lotus-stalks from this pond. (She exits and returns, in dramatic gesture placing lotus-leaves on <s>Sāgarikā</s>'s heart.)
(2.19) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! Take away these lotus-leaves and lotus-stalks. Enough of this. Why do you torment yourself without reason? For listen:
[Verse 26:] Shame from love for an unattainable person, heavy is the burden, the self subject to another's will — / Dear friend, love is cruel; death alone is the one refuge.
Thus she faints.
(2.20) (Commotion offstage.)
[Verse 27:] With the remnant of a golden chain cut at the neck, dragging below a chain-link garland, / having leapt over the doors, with a circle of tinkling bells ringing at his carelessly moving feet, / having alarmed the women, pursued on his path by horse-keepers in confusion, / this escaped monkey enters the king's palace from the stable.
And moreover:
[Verse 28:] Having lost his way from being pelted with showers, abandoning shame due to the absence of human reckoning, / this dwarf enters inside the chamberlain's tunic out of fear. / The border-dwelling <s>Kirātas</s>, fitting to his own name, / the hunchbacks slowly go, suspecting they themselves are being looked at, out of their very lowness.
(2.21) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (hearing, with alarm): Friend! Get up, get up! That wicked monkey is coming right this way!
(2.22) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: What shall I do now?
(2.23) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Come! Let us enter the doorway of this <s>tamāla</s>-grove and wait this out. (They walk around and stand aside.)
(2.24) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! What? You've left the painting-board behind! Someone might see it!
(2.25) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Oh well done! What will you do with the painting-board even now? This wicked monkey, being greedy for curds and rice, has broken open this cage and escaped! That <s>Medhāvinī</s> has flown away elsewhere! So come, let us quickly follow her.
(2.26) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! Let us do so. (They walk about.)
(2.27) (Offstage): Oh oh! Amazing, amazing!
(2.28) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (looking with fear): <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! It seems the wicked monkey is coming again!
(2.29) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (looking, laughing): Oh timid one! Don't be afraid! This is <s>Vasantaka</s>, the lord's companion residing in the palace, today being the spring festival.
Then enters the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester).
(2.30) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Oh oh! Amazing, amazing! Well done, <s>Śrīkaṇṭhadāsa</s>, you righteous one, well done!
(2.31) <s>Sāgarikā</s> gazes with longing.
(2.32) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! What use is this sight? The mynah bird has gone far away! So let us follow her. (They exit.)
(2.33) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Well done, <s>Śrīkaṇṭhadāsa</s>, well done! By whose mere assigned task such a flower-creeper has come about — whose branches are continuously covered with bursting flower-clusters, appearing as if laughing — the queen's personal <s>Mādhavī</s>-creeper! So let me go and report to my dear friend. (Walking about and looking) Here comes my dear friend himself, having received the fulfillment of that task; though the creeper blossomed out of his sight, gazing at it as if it were before his eyes, his eyes wide with delight — he comes right this way! So let me approach him. (He goes toward the king.)
Then enters the King as described.
(2.34) King (with delight):
[Verse 29:] With unrestrained buds, its pale-white hue, having begun to bloom in a moment, / spreading its own languor through incessant gusts of breeze — / seeing this garden-creeper today, this other passionate woman as it were, / I shall surely make the queen's face flush with jealousy.
(2.35) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (approaching quickly): Victory, victory to my dear friend! O master! Your fortune increases! By whose mere [instruction]... (He reads again.)
(2.36) King: What doubt? Indeed, the power of gems, mantras, and herbs is inconceivable. So show the way by which we too may reap the fruit of our eyes through beholding it.
(2.37) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (with pomp): Come, come, sir! (They both walk about.)
(2.38) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (hearing, fearfully turning back, seizing the king's hand with alarm): O master! Come! Let us flee!
(2.39) King: For what reason?
(2.40) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! Some ghost dwells in this <s>bakula</s> tree!
(2.41) King: Shame on you, fool! Go forward confidently. How could such things exist here?
(2.42) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: It speaks in perfectly clear syllables! If you don't believe my words, then go ahead and listen for yourself!
(2.43) King (doing so and hearing):
[Verse 30:] Clear in syllables, sweet by feminine nature, / resonating softly due to its small body — / I think the mynah bird speaks.
(Looking up, smiling) Indeed, a mynah bird.
(2.44) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking up): What! It really is a mynah bird!
(2.45) King (laughing): Just so.
(2.46) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! You are fortunate indeed — you who say it's a mynah bird while I thought it was a ghost!
(2.47) King: Shame on you, fool! What you yourself did, you attribute to me!
(2.48) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! If that's so, don't restrain me! (Angrily raising his stick) Ho, slave-girl's daughter, mynah bird! You know: 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is truly to be feared!' So wait! With this stick, crooked like the heart of a tale-bearing person, I shall knock you down from this <s>bakula</s> tree like a ripe fruit! (He raises the stick to strike.)
(2.49) King (stopping him): She is saying something charming! So why are you frightening her? Let us listen. (They listen.)
(2.50) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! She says: 'Friend! Who is this drawn by you?' 'Friend! It is the spring-festival Lord <s>Anaṅga</s>.' And again she says: 'Friend! Why have you drawn me here?' 'Friend! Why are you angry without reason? Just as you drew the God of Love, so I drew <s>Rati</s>. So, you who suspect otherwise — what use is this evasion? Tell me the whole story.' Sir! What is this about?
(2.51) King: Friend! I surmise thus: some woman has drawn her heart's beloved out of love, and concealed it under the pretext of the God of Love. Her friend too recognized him, and with cleverness drew herself there as well under the pretext of <s>Rati</s>.
(2.52) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (snapping his fingers): That does make sense!
(2.53) King: Friend! Be silent! She speaks again.
(2.54) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (listening again): Sir! She says: 'Don't be ashamed, don't be ashamed! It is only natural that one of such ear-pleasing beauty should desire such a worthy match.' Sir! The one who was drawn must be a man handsome enough to delight the ears!
(2.55) King: If so, let us listen attentively. There is room for our curiosity.
(2.56) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (listening again): Sir! Did you hear what she said? 'Friend! Take away these lotus-leaves and lotus-stalks. Enough of this. Why do you torment yourself without reason?'
(2.57) King: Friend! Not only have I heard, but the intent is clearly discerned.
(2.58) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! Don't be puffed up with your cleverness! I, having heard everything, will explain it to you. Let us listen first. What is the slave-girl's daughter, the mynah bird, murmuring about?
(2.59) King: Well spoken! (They listen again.)
(2.60) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! That slave-girl's daughter, the mynah bird, like a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> learned in the four <s>Vedas</s>, has begun reciting verses!
(2.61) King: Friend! Being distracted, I did not hear properly. So tell me — what else was said?
(2.62) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! She recited this: 'Unattainable...' (He reads again.)
(2.63) King (laughing): Well done, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, well done! Who else besides a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> like you could be versed in such verses?
(2.64) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: What is this now?
(2.65) King: Fool! This is a verse! It was spoken by some woman of praiseworthy youth, unable to attain her beloved, with no regard for her own life.
(2.66) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (laughing loudly): Ahaha! What use are these roundabout words? Why don't you just say directly: 'by one unable to attain me'? Otherwise, who else would be concealed under the pretext of the Flower-Bowed One? (Laughing loudly) Ahaha!
(2.67) King (looking up): Shame on you, fool! By laughing so loudly you have frightened her so that she has flown off somewhere from here!
(2.68) Both look about.
(2.69) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking): Sir! She has gone to the banana-grove! So let us quickly follow!
(2.70) King: So be it. (Walking about.)
[Verse 31:] What was spoken by a woman bearing the irresistible pain of Love's arrow / before her friends — / that, when repeated by young parrots and mynah birds, / attains the status of an unexpected guest at the ears of the fortunate.
(2.71) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! This is the banana-grove. Let us enter. (They both enter.)
(2.72) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: What need of that slave-girl's daughter, the mynah bird! Here, let us sit for a moment on this stone slab, cool with banana-leaves gently swaying in the soft breeze, and rest awhile.
(2.73) King: As it pleases you. (They sit.)
(2.74) The King reads 'The irresistible...' etc. again.
(2.75) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking to the side): But this must be the cage of that mynah bird, with its door open!
(2.76) King: Friend! Let us examine it.
(2.77) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: As my lord commands. (Walking about and looking) Here is also a painting-board! Let me take it! (Taking the board and examining it, with delight) Sir! Your fortune increases!
(2.78) King (with curiosity): Friend! What is this?
(2.79) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! This is just what I told you! You yourself are drawn here! Otherwise, who else would be concealed under the pretext of the Flower-Bowed One?
(2.80) King (with delight, extending both hands): Friend! Show me!
(2.81) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! I won't show it! That beauty too is drawn right here! So should such an eye-delighting painting be shown without a reward?
(2.82) King (handing over a bracelet, forcibly taking [the board], looking with amazement): Friend!
[Verse 32:] This woman, playfully brushing aside the lotus, / declaring her partiality toward us — / enters my mind like a royal swan / gone into a painting.
Moreover:
[Verse 33:] Having created this unprecedented full-moon face of hers, / the Creator <s>Dhātā</s> surely became / uncomfortable from the closing of the lotus that is his own seat.
Then enter <s>Sāgarikā</s> and <s>Susaṃgatā</s>.
(2.83) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! The mynah bird has not been found. So let us at least take the painting-board from this banana-grove and go quickly.
(2.84) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! Let us do so. (They approach.)
(2.85) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! But why has she been drawn with downcast face?
(2.86) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (hearing): Friend! From what <s>Vasantaka</s> says, I infer that the lord must be right here too! So let us hide behind the banana plants and watch. (Both listen.)
(2.87) King: Friend! Look, look! (He reads 'Having created this unprecedented...' etc. again.)
(2.88) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! Your fortune increases! Your beloved is describing none other than you!
(2.89) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! Why do you make light of me with such jesting in this matter?
(2.90) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (nudging the king): I'm asking — why has she been drawn with downcast face?
(2.91) King: Friend! Didn't the mynah bird already reveal everything?
(2.92) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: <s>Medhāvinī</s> has truly demonstrated her cleverness!
(2.93) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! Does this woman please your eyes or not?
(2.94) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (with apprehension, aside): What will he say? I stand truly between death and life on this account!
(2.95) King: Friend! What can be said? She overwhelms! Look:
[Verse 34:] My gaze, having with difficulty passed beyond her pair of thighs, / having long wandered on the slopes of her hips, / in the middle, amid the rough waves of her three waist-folds, having come to a standstill — / now slowly climbing her high breasts, like one who is thirsty, / gazes repeatedly, full of longing, at her eyes streaming with drops of water.
(2.96) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! Did you hear?
(2.97) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Friend! You alone listen — you whose knowledge of paintings is being praised!
(2.98) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! For one before whom even such women honor the joy of meeting with their beloved, what disrespect can there be toward yourself, that you do not see your own self drawn by her?
(2.99) King (examining): Friend! That I was drawn by her — this truth now fills me with self-regard. But how can I not see?
[Verse 35:] The shower of drops from the tears of her who was drawing this, / that fell upon the board, appears / like beads of perspiration on my body / arising from the very touch of her hand.
(2.100) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (aside): Heart! Be comforted, be comforted! Your wish has not yet reached that extent.
(2.101) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! You alone are to be praised, who so satisfies the lord!
(2.102) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking to the side): Sir! Here is something else — it appears to be her own token of lovesickness, made of fresh lotus-pond leaves and lotus-stalks.
(2.103) King: Keenly observed! For:
[Verse 36:] Wilted on both sides from contact with her full breasts and broad hips, / having failed to reach the green skin of her middle, / this bed of lotus-leaves, with its loose spreading vine-like arms tossed about, / speaks of the torment of the slender-bodied one with its disarranged placement.
Moreover:
[Verse 37:] This broad lotus-leaf placed upon her chest / does not so much reveal her inner state of lovesickness / as it proclaims, by its two circles / — shrunk by the heat of her excessive burning — / the girth of her pair of breasts.
(2.104) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (picking up a lotus-stalk in dramatic gesture): Sir! Here is another thing — her soft lotus-stalk necklace, soiled by pressing against her full breasts! So let the lord look!
(2.105) King (taking it and placing it on his own chest): O dull-natured one!
[Verse 38:] O lotus-stalk necklace, fallen from the center of her pitcher-like breasts, / why do you wither? / Even for your slender fiber, / how could there be room there?
(2.106) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (aside): Oh dear, oh dear! The lord, his heart seized by love for my mistress, has begun speaking distractedly! So it is not proper to observe further. So be it for now. (Aloud) Friend! The one for whose sake you came — he stands before you!
(2.107) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (with jealousy): <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! For whose sake have I come?
(2.108) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (laughing): Oh suspicious one! For the painting-board, of course! So take it.
(2.109) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (angrily): <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! I've had enough of such talk from you! I'm leaving! (She starts to go.)
(2.110) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (taking hold of <s>Sāgarikā</s>): Oh impatient one! Just wait here a moment while I go into this banana-grove and bring back the painting-board! (She enters the banana-grove.)
(2.111) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (seeing <s>Susaṃgatā</s>, with alarm): Sir! Hide the painting-board! Here comes <s>Susaṃgatā</s>, the queen's attendant!
(2.112) The King covers the board with the edge of his garment.
(2.113) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (approaching): Victory, victory to the lord!
(2.114) King: <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! How did you know I was here?
(2.115) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Lord! Not only you — together with the painting-board, the entire affair has been discovered by me! So I shall go and report to the queen! (She starts to go.)
(2.116) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (aside, fearfully): Sir! Everything is possible! She is a shrewd maidservant! So please appease her!
(2.117) King: Well spoken! (Taking <s>Susaṃgatā</s>'s hand) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! This is merely play! Even so, there is no need for you to vex the queen without cause. (He offers an ear-ornament.)
(2.118) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (bowing, with a smile): Lord! Be free of suspicion! I too was merely playing, by the lord's grace! So what need of the ear-ornament? This alone is my great reward — that my dear friend <s>Sāgarikā</s>, who was angry saying 'Why have you drawn me here on the painting-board?' — let her alone be appeased!
(2.119) King (rising with excitement): Where is she? Where is she?
(2.120) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Come, come, my lord! (All rise.)
(2.121) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! I'll take the painting-board! It may prove useful again sometime. (All exit from the banana-grove.)
(2.122) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (seeing the King, with delight, apprehension, and trembling, to herself): Oh dear, oh dear! Seeing this, I cannot move even a single step! So what shall I do now?
(2.123) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (seeing <s>Sāgarikā</s>): Amazing, amazing! Is such beauty to be found in the world of mortals? I think even the Creator himself, having fashioned this, must have been struck with wonder!
(2.124) King: Friend! My mind too is of the very same thought:
[Verse 39:] The eyes were widened, surpassing the splendor of their own lotus-petals; / 'Well done! Well done!' was uttered in unison by all four faces; / heads were shaken in amazement — surely by <s>Brahmā</s> the Creator, / having fashioned this woman, the ornament of the three worlds, who never was before.
(2.125) <s>Sāgarikā</s> (looking at <s>Susaṃgatā</s> with jealousy): <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Such is the painting-board you have brought! (She starts to go.)
(2.126) King:
[Verse 40:] Though you cast your gaze in anger, O beautiful one, / it will come only affectionately and never in harshness. / Abandon your haste and go — by the stumbling of your feet, / this heavy weight of your hips will bring you great fatigue.
(2.127) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Lord! She is extremely angry! So take her by the hand and appease her!
(2.128) King (with delight): As you say! (Taking <s>Sāgarikā</s>'s hand, he acts out the touch.)
(2.129) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! You have now obtained a new splendor!
(2.130) King: Friend! Truly so.
[Verse 41:] This is <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) herself — and this hand of hers is the sprout of the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree. / How else could this drop of nectar fall, disguised as perspiration?
O beautiful one! Be gracious! It is not proper to maintain such continued anger in the company of friends.
(2.131) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! You are ungracious now, if even when held by the hand by the lord, you still do not release your anger!
(2.132) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Here comes the other queen, <s>Vāsavadattā</s>!
(2.133) The King, startled, releases <s>Sāgarikā</s>.
(2.134) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! What shall I do now?
(2.135) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Friend! Let us conceal ourselves behind this row of <s>tamāla</s> trees and slip away. (They exit.)
(2.136) King (looking about with amazement): Friend! Where is Queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>?
(2.137) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: What I said was: 'Here comes the other Queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>' — meaning she has become extremely prolonged in her anger!
(2.138) King: Shame on you, fool!
[Verse 42:] Somehow obtained through fate, drawn close to my neck, radiant with unconcealed passion — / like a gem-necklace (<s>Ratnāvalī</s>), that beautiful woman / has been made to slip from my hand by you!
Then enter <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>.
(2.139) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! How far away now is that <s>Navamalikā</s> creeper tended by the prince?
(2.140) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady! It will be visible just past this banana-grove! So come, my lady! (They walk about.)
(2.141) King: Friend! Where now shall I see my beloved?
(2.142) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady! From the way the lord speaks nearby, I think he is standing here waiting for you! So approach, my lady!
(2.143) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (approaching): Victory, victory to my lord!
(2.144) King (aside): Friend! Cover the painting-board!
(2.145) The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> takes it and covers it with his upper garment.
(2.146) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: My lord! The <s>Navamalikā</s> has blossomed!
(2.147) King: Queen! Even though we came first, you took so long that we have not yet seen it. So come! Let us both look together.
(2.148) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (examining his face): By the expression on my lord's face alone I have learned that the <s>Navamalikā</s> has blossomed! So I shall not go.
(2.149) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: My lady! If that's the case, then we have won! (He spreads his arms and dances; the board falls from under his arm; he acts dismayed.)
(2.150) The King, aside, threatens the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> with his finger.
(2.151) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (aside): Sir! Don't be angry! I myself will handle this!
(2.152) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> (picking up the board): Look, look, my lady! What is drawn here?
(2.153) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (examining): This is my lord! And this too is <s>Sāgarikā</s>! (To the king) My lord! What is this?
(2.154) King (aside with embarrassment): Friend! What shall I say?
(2.155) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: My lady! Hearing my words that 'one's own self is difficult to draw,' my dear friend demonstrated this skill.
(2.156) King: It is just as <s>Vasantaka</s> says.
(2.157) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (pointing at the board): My lord! And this other woman who appears near you — is this too the skill of <s>Vasantaka</s>?
(2.158) King (with an embarrassed smile): Queen! Please don't misconstrue this! This one was imagined and drawn by me from my own mind alone — she has never been seen before.
(2.159) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: My lady! Truly! I swear by my <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood that such a one has never been seen before!
(2.160) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> (aside): My lady! Even chance scratches of woodworms sometimes ring true.
(2.161) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (aside): Oh honest one! This is <s>Vasantaka</s> — don't you know his roundabout speech? (Aloud) My lord! But from looking at this painting-board, a headache has come upon me! So I shall go.
(2.162) King (taking the edge of her garment): Queen!
[Verse 43:] I would say 'Be pleased' — but that does not fit when there is no anger; / 'I shall never do it again' — that would be an admission of guilt; / 'There is no fault of mine' — you will know even this to be false; / what is fitting to say in this case — I do not know, O beloved!
(2.163) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (modestly drawing away the garment edge): My lord! Do not misconstrue! Truly a headache has come upon me! So I shall go. (They exit.)
(2.164) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Sir! Your fortune increases! By good luck, the storm of talk has passed over us safely!
(2.165) King: Shame on you, fool! Be content! Due to your lack of subtlety, you failed to notice the concealed thread of the queen's anger! For:
[Verse 44:] Even when her brow suddenly furrowed, her face was brought to the utmost modesty; / the slightly betraying smile toward me was not expressed, nor harsh words spoken; / the eye, made stiff by inner tears, was not opened wide — through dignity; / anger was displayed by my beloved, yet courtesy was never abandoned.
So come! Let us go to the queen. (They exit.)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second act.

body.text:
tataḥ praviśati madanikā |
(3.1) Madanikā | ākāśe | kosambie | avi diṭṭhā tae bhaṭṭiṇīsaāse kañcaṇamālā ṇa vā | ākarṇya | kiṃ bhaṇāsi | ko vi kālo tāe āacchia gadāe tti | tā kahiṃ dāṇiṃ pekkhissaṃ | agrato 'valokya | esā khu kañcaṇamālā ido jjevva āacchadi | tā jāva uvasappāmi |
tataḥ praviati kāñcanamālā |
(3.2) Kāñcanamālā | sotprāsam | sāhu re vasantaa sāhu | adisaido tae amaccajoandharāaṇao imāe saṃdhiviggahacintāe |
(3.3) Madanikā | upasṛtya sasmitam | halā kañcaṇamāle | kiṃ ajjavasantaeṇa kadaṃ jeṇa so evvaṃ salāhīadi |
(3.4) Kāñcanamālā | halā maaṇie | kiṃ tuha ediṇā pucchideṇa paoaṇaṃ | ṇa tumaṃ imaṃ rahassaṃ rakkhiduṃ pāresi |
(3.5) Madanikā | savāmi devīe caraṇehiṃ jai kassa vi purado paāsemi |
(3.6) Kāñcanamālā | jai evvaṃ tā suṇaṃ | ajja kkhu mae rāaulādo paḍiṇivattantīe cittasāliāduvāre ajjavasantaassa susaṃgadāe samaṃ ālāvo sudo |
(3.7) Madanikā | sakautukaṃ | sahi | kīdiso |
(3.8) Kāñcanamālā | jadhā | susaṃgade | ṇa kkhu sāariaṃ vajjia piavaassassa kiṃ pi assatthadāe kāraṇaṃ | tā cintehi ettha paḍiāraṃ ti |
(3.9) Madanikā | tado susaṃgadāe kiṃ bhaṇidaṃ |
(3.10) Kāñcanamālā | evvaṃ bhaṇidaṃ | ajja kkhu devīe cittaphalaavuttantasaṅkidāe sāariaṃ rakkhiduṃ mama hatthe samappaantīe jaṃ ṇevatthaṃ me pasādīkidaṃ teṇa jjevva viraidadevīvesaṃ sāariaṃ geṇhia ahaṃ pi kañcaṇamālāvesadhāriṇī bhavia padīse idha āgamissaṃ | tumaṃ pi cittasāliāduvāre maṃ paḍivālaissasi | tado māhavīladāmaṇḍave tāe saha bhaṭṭiṇo saṃgamo bhavissadi tti |
(3.11) Madanikā | hadāsā tumaṃ susaṃgade jā evvaṃ pariaṇavacchalaṃ deviṃ vañcesi |
(3.12) Kāñcanamālā | halā | tumaṃ dāṇiṃ kahiṃ patthidā |
(3.13) Madanikā | assatthasarīrassa bhaṭṭiṇo kusalavuttantaṃ jāṇiduṃ gadā tumaṃ ciraasi tti uttammantīe devīe pesida mhi |
(3.14) Kāñcanamālā | adiujjuā dāṇiṃ devī jā evvaṃ pattiāadi | parikramyāvalokya ca | eso kkhu bhaṭṭā assatthadāmiseṇa attaṇo maaṇāvatthaṃ pacchādaanto dantatoraṇavaḍabhīe uvaviṭṭho ciṭṭhadi | tā ehi | edaṃ vuttantaṃ bhaṭṭiṇīe ṇivedemha |
iti niṣkrānte |
iti praveśakaḥ |
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Madanikā</s> enters.
(3.1) <s>Madanikā</s> (addressing someone offstage): <s>Kosambī</s>! Has <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> been seen by you at the queen's residence, or not? (Listening) What do you say? That she left some time ago? Then where shall I look for her now? (Looking ahead) Ah, here comes <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> this way. Let me approach her.
Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> enters.
(3.2) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> (with surprise): Bravo, <s>Vasantaka</s>, bravo! Minister <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> has been surpassed by you in this scheming of alliance and hostility!
(3.3) <s>Madanikā</s> (approaching with a smile): Friend <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! What has noble <s>Vasantaka</s> done that he is so praised?
(3.4) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: Friend <s>Madanikā</s>! What use is it for you to ask about this? You will not be able to keep this secret.
(3.5) <s>Madanikā</s>: I swear by the queen's feet — I shall not reveal it before anyone.
(3.6) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: If so, then listen. Today, as I was returning from the royal palace, at the door of the <s>Citrasālā</s> (painting gallery), I overheard a conversation of noble <s>Vasantaka</s> with <s>Susaṃgatā</s>.
(3.7) <s>Madanikā</s> (with curiosity): Friend, what kind?
(3.8) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: As follows: "<s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Apart from <s>Sāgarikā</s>, there is truly no other cause for the master's illness. So think of a remedy for this."
(3.9) <s>Madanikā</s>: Then what did <s>Susaṃgatā</s> say?
(3.10) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: She said thus: "Today, the queen, suspecting the truth about the <s>Citraphala</s> (painting) incident, has entrusted <s>Sāgarikā</s> to me for safekeeping — and thereby inadvertently shown me favor. Therefore, I shall take <s>Sāgarikā</s> wearing the queen's attire while I myself assume the guise of <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, and bring her here at night. You too should wait for me at the door of the <s>Citrasālā</s>. Then, in the <s>Mādhavīlatā</s> (jasmine) pavilion, the meeting of the master with her will take place."
(3.11) <s>Madanikā</s>: Alas, <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! You are indeed shameless, who thus deceive the queen under the pretext of loyal service!
(3.12) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: Friend! Where are you going now?
(3.13) <s>Madanikā</s>: I was sent by the queen, who is anxious, to learn the news of the well-being of the ailing master.
(3.14) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: The queen is exceedingly trusting, who believes thus! (Walking about and looking) There is the master, seated on the balcony of the ivory gateway, concealing his lovesickness under the pretext of illness. Come then! Let us report this matter to the queen.
They exit.
Thus ends the <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene).

tataḥ praviśati gṛhītaratnamālā susaṃgatā |
(4.1) Susaṃgatā | sakaruṇam | hā piasahi sāarie | hā lajjālue | hā sahījaṇavacchale | hā udārasīle | hā sommadaṃsaṇe | kahiṃ dāṇiṃ tumaṃ mae pekkhidavvā | iti roditi | ūrdhvam avalokya niḥśvasya ca | ai devvahadaa | jai sā asāmaṇṇarūvasohā tādisī tae ṇimmidā tā kīsa uṇa īdisaṃ avatthantaraṃ pāvidā | iaṃ ca raaṇamālā jīvidaṇirāsāe tāe kassa vi bamhaṇassa hatthe paḍivādesu tti bhaṇia mama hatthe samappidā | tā jāva kaṃ pi bamhaṇaṃ aṇṇesāmi | parikramyāvalokya ca | eso kkhu ajjavasantao ido jjevva āacchadi | tā jāva edassa jjevva paḍivādaissaṃ |
tataḥ praviśati hṛṣṭo vasantakaḥ |
(4.2) Vidūṣakaḥ | hī hī bho | ajja kkhu piavaasseṇa pasādidāe devīe vāsavadattāe bandhaṇādo moāvia sahatthadiṇṇehiṃ modaehiṃ udaraṃ me pūridaṃ | aṇṇaṃ ca | paṭṭaṃsuajualaṃ kaṇṇāharaṃ ca diṇṇaṃ | tā jāva piavaassaṃ pekkhāmi |
(4.3) Susaṃgatā | rudatī sahasopasṛtya | ajjavasantaa | ciṭṭha dāva |
(4.4) Vidūṣakaḥ | dṛṣṭvā | kadhaṃ | susaṃgadā | bhodi susaṃgade | kiṃ ṇimittaṃ rodīadi | kiṃ ṇu sāariāe accāhidaṃ saṃvuttaṃ |

body.translated_text: Then <s>Susaṃgatā</s> enters, holding the jewel necklace. (4.1) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (with compassion): Oh, dear friend <s>Sāgarikā</s>! Oh, modest one! Oh, gentle one to your companions! Oh, noble-natured one! Oh, beautiful to behold! Where now shall I see you? (She weeps.) (Looking upward and sighing) O fate! If you created her with such extraordinary beauty of form, then why has she been brought to such a pitiable state? And this jewel necklace — she, despairing of life, said 'Give it as a gift to some <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' and placed it in my hands. So let me seek some <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (Walking about and looking) Here comes the noble <s>Vasantaka</s> this way. So let me give it to him. (Then <s>Vasantaka</s> enters, delighted.) (4.2) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Ha ha! Today the queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, pleased by my dear friend [the king], having had me released from prison, has filled my stomach with sweetmeats given by her own hand. And moreover, she has given me a silk garment and ear-ornaments. So let me go see my dear friend. (4.3) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (weeping, approaching suddenly): Noble <s>Vasantaka</s>! Wait a moment! (4.4) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (looking): What — <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Lady <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! Why are you weeping? Has something happened to <s>Sāgarikā</s>? (4.5) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: This is what I shall report. That ascetic woman — a rumor was spread that she was sent by the queen to <s>Ujjayinī</s>, but at midnight, having stood there, no one knows where she was taken. (4.6) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (with alarm): Oh, lady <s>Sāgarikā</s>! The queen has acted most cruelly! (4.7) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: And this jewel necklace — she, despairing of life, said 'Give it as a gift to the noble <s>Vasantaka</s>' and placed it in my hands. So let the noble one accept this. (4.8) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (with compassion): In such a plight, my hands do not extend to take this. (Both weep.) (4.9) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> (with folded hands): Let the noble one accept it, doing a favor for her sake. (4.10) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (reflecting): But on the other hand, bring it here — with this very thing I shall console my dear friend who is grieving from separation from <s>Sāgarikā</s>. (4.11) <s>Susaṃgatā</s> hands it over. (4.12) <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (having taken it and examining it with wonder): <s>Susaṃgatā</s>! From where did she get such an ornament? (4.13) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Noble one, I too asked her this very thing out of curiosity. (4.14) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Then what did she say? (4.15) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Then she, looking upward and sighing deeply, said '<s>Susaṃgatā</s>, what use to you is this story?' and began to weep. (4.16) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: This is precisely what one would expect — by this ornament, which is beyond the reach of common folk, she must certainly be of noble birth. <s>Susaṃgatā</s>, where is my dear friend now? (4.17) <s>Susaṃgatā</s>: Noble one, the master, having come out of the queen's chambers, has gone to the crystal-stone pavilion. So let the noble one go. And I too shall attend upon the queen. (Both exit.) Thus ends the <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene).

body.translated_text: Then enters <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>, sword in hand. (4.38) <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>: [Approaching.] "Victory, victory to the lord! Here, the beloved brother-in-law <s>Vijayavarmā</s> of <s>Rumaṇvat</s> stands at the gate, wishing to report something." (4.39) The King: <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>, bring him in without delay. (4.40) <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>: "As the lord commands." [Exits, then re-enters with <s>Vijayavarmā</s>.] "<s>Vijayavarmā</s>, here is the lord. Approach the master." (4.41) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: [Approaching.] "Victory, victory to the lord! Sire, may you prosper — congratulations on <s>Rumaṇvat</s>'s victory!" (4.42) The King: [With satisfaction.] <s>Vijayavarmā</s>, have the <s>Kosalas</s> been conquered? (4.43) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: By the lord's grace. (4.44) The King: Well done, <s>Rumaṇvat</s>, well done! A great purpose has been accomplished in a short time. <s>Vijayavarmā</s>, then tell us the story — I wish to hear it in full detail. (4.45) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: Sire, listen! By the lord's command, within just a few days, <s>Rumaṇvat</s> set forth with a great army of manifold cavalry, elephants, and infantry — irresistible — and reaching the gate of the king of <s>Kosala</s>, who was stationed in the <s>Vindhya</s> fortress, began to encamp. (4.46) The King: Then what? Then what? (4.47) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: Then the king of <s>Kosala</s> too, unable to endure the insult out of pride, prepared his army, which consisted mostly of elephants. (4.48) The <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: "<s>Vijayavarmā</s>! Tell quickly! My heart is trembling!" (4.49) The King: Then what? Then what? (4.50) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: Sire, having made his resolve, "Emerging from the <s>Vindhya</s> to fight, he stood facing [the enemy]. At that very instant, blocking the directions like another <s>Vindhya</s> range with the confinement of his elephant army, rapidly releasing arrows — then, his infantry crushed by maddened war-elephants, falling upon [the foe], <s>Rumaṇvat</s>, with zeal doubled by the attainment of his desire, drove him back in an instant." || 68 || And further: "When in the battlefield, with heads repeatedly severed by the clash of weapons and armor, in the river of streaming blood, amid fire vomited by the heat [of battle], having been challenged, the king of <s>Kosala</s>, with his chief army broken —" (4.51) The King: What! Were our forces also broken? (4.52) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: "— by <s>Rumaṇvat</s> alone, mounted on his maddened elephant, was slain with hundreds of arrows." || 69 || (4.53) The <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: "Victory, victory to you! We have won!" [He dances.] (4.54) The King: Well done, O king of <s>Kosala</s>, well done! Even your death is praiseworthy, since even your enemies thus describe your valor. (4.55) <s>Vijayavarmā</s>: <s>Rumaṇvat</s> also, having installed my elder brother <s>Jayavarmā</s> over the <s>Kosalas</s>, followed by the remnant of his entire army — mostly elephants — wounded in battle, is gradually returning. (4.56) The King: <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>, tell <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: let my royal favor be given to him. (4.57) <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>: "As the lord commands." [Exits with <s>Vijayavarmā</s>.]
