Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> enters.
(4.58) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: I have been commanded by the queen thus: 'Dear <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, go and show this magician to the noble lord.' (Walking about and looking) There is the master. Let me approach him. (Approaching) Victory, victory to the lord! Lord, the queen humbly reports: 'A magician named <s>Sambarasiddhi</s> has arrived from <s>Ujjayinī</s>. Let the noble lord watch him.'
(4.59) King: We are curious about the magician. Bring him in quickly.
(4.60) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: As the lord commands. (Exits and re-enters with the magician holding a peacock-feather fan in hand) Come, come, sir.
(4.61) The magician walks about.
(4.62) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: There is the master. Approach, sir.
(4.63) The magician: Victory, victory to the lord! (Approaching and waving the peacock-feather fan)
Bow at the feet of <s>Indra</s>, who gained his name in the realm of illusion,
and likewise of noble <s>Sambara</s>, whose glory is established in the aerial chariots. || 70 || (4.7)
Sire:
Shall there be a mirage-deer on the earth, a mountain on water, fire on water,
or darkness at midday? Give the command! || 71 || (4.8)
(4.64) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Dear friend! He is not a fraud! Sir! Such is his confidence that he claims to accomplish everything!
(4.65) The magician: Sire:
What need of much talk? Whatever you wish to see in your heart,
that very thing I shall show you, by the power of my guru's <s>mantras</s> (spells). || 72 || (4.9)
(4.66) King: <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! Tell the queen: 'This magician is indeed yours, and this place has been cleared of people. So come — together we shall watch him.'
(4.67) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: As the lord commands. (Exits and re-enters with <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.)
(4.68) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Dear <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! Since he has come from <s>Ujjayinī</s>, I feel a fondness for this magician.
(4.69) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: This shows the queen's respect for her birth-family. So come, my lady.
They walk about.
(4.70) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: My lady, there is the master. Let the queen approach.
(4.71) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> (approaching): Victory, victory to the noble lord!
(4.72) King: My queen, he has boasted much. So let us watch him right from where we are seated.
(4.73) <s>Vāsavadattā</s> sits down.
(4.74) King: Good sir, begin your display of the various magical illusions.
(4.75) The magician: As the lord commands. (Having performed various theatrical acts, waving the peacock-feather fan)
I show you the court of the gods, with <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> as chief deities,
and dancing in the sky, with many hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Vidyādharas</s>. || 73 || (4.10)
All watch with amazement.
(4.76) King (looking upward, rising from his seat): Marvelous! Marvelous!
(4.77) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Marvelous! Marvelous!
(4.78) King: My queen, look!
Here is <s>Brahmā</s> on his lotus; this is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, bearing the crescent moon as his crest;
this is the slayer of <s>Daityas</s>, with four arms bearing the marks of bow, sword, mace, and discus;
and this is <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, mounted on <s>Airāvata</s>; these, O Queen, are the other gods;
and dancing in the sky are these divine women, with anklets jingling on their moving feet. || 74 || (4.11)
(4.79) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Marvelous! Marvelous!
(4.80) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: O slave-girl's son, magician! What use are these gods and celestial nymphs you have shown? If you are content with this much, then show us <s>Sāgarikā</s>!

(4.176) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | karotv āsanaparigrahaṃ devaḥ | sarvaṃ vijñāpayāmi |
sarva upaviśanti |
(4.177) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | deva | śruyatām | yeyaṃ siṃhaleśvaraduhitā sā siddhenādiṣṭā yathā | yo 'syāḥ pāṇigrahaṇaṃ kariṣyati sa sārvabhaumo rājā bhaviṣyatīti | tatas tatpratyayād asmābhiḥ svāmino 'rthe bahuśaḥ prārthyamānenāpi siṃhaleśvareṇa devyā vāsavadattāyāś cittakhedaṃ pariharatā yadā na dattā |
(4.178) Rājā | tadā kim |
(4.179) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | tadā lāvaṇake devī dagdheti prasiddhim utpādya tadantikaṃ bābhravyaḥ prahitaḥ |
(4.180) Rājā | yaugandharāyaṇa | ataḥ paraṃ śrutam eva mayā | atheyaṃ devīhaste kim ity anucintya sthāpitā |
(4.181) Vidūṣakaḥ | aṇācakkhidaṃ pi edaṃ jāṇīadi jjevva jadhā | anteuragadā suheṇa de daṃsaṇapadhaṃ gamissadi tti |
(4.182) Rājā | gṛhīto 'bhiprāyas te vasantakena |
(4.183) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | yathājñāpayati devaḥ |
(4.184) Rājā | aindrajālikavṛttānto 'pi manye tvatprayoga eva |
(4.185) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | anyathāntaḥpure baddhāyā asyāḥ kuto devena darśanam | adṛṣṭāyāś ca vasubhūtinā kutaḥ parijñānam | vihasya | parijñātāyāś ca bhaginyāḥ saṃprati yathā karaṇīyaṃ tatra devī pramāṇam |
(4.186) Vāsavadattā | ajjautta | phuḍāṃ jevva kiṃ ṇa bhaṇāsi jadhā | paḍivādehi me raaṇāvaliṃ ti |
(4.187) Vidūṣakaḥ | bhodi | suṭṭhu tae jāṇido amaccassa ahippāo |
(4.188) Vāsavadattā | ehi raaṇāvali ehi | ettiaṃ pi dāva mama bahiṇiāṇurūvaṃ bhodu | iti ratnāvalīṃ svakīyair ābharaṇair alaṅkṛtya haste gṛhītvā rājānam upasṛtya | ajjautta | edaṃ raaṇāvaliṃ paḍiccha |
(4.189) Rājā | saharṣaṃ hastau prasārya | ko devyāḥ prasādaṃ na bahu manyate |
(4.190) Vāsavadattā | ajjautta | dūre kkhu edāe ṇādikulaṃ | tā tadhā karesu jadhā bandhujaṇaṃ ṇa sumaredi | iti samarpayati |
(4.191) Rājā | yathājñāpayati devī |
(4.192) Vidūṣakaḥ | saharṣaṃ nṛtyati | hī hī bho | jaadu jaadu bhavaṃ | puḍhavī khu dāṇiṃ hatthagadā piavaassassa |
(4.193) Vasubhūtiḥ | devi | sthāne devīśabdam udvahasi |
(4.194) Bābhravyaḥ | idānīṃ saphalapariśramo 'smi saṃvṛttaḥ |
(4.195) Yaugandharāyaṇaḥ | deva | kiṃ te bhūyaḥ priyam upakaromi |
(4.196) Rājā | kim ataḥ param api priyam asti | yataḥ |
nīto vikramabāhur ātmasamatāṃ prāpteyam urvītale
sāraṃ sāgarikā sasāgaramahīprāpty ekahetuḥ priyā |
devī prītim upāgatā ca bhaginīlābhāj jitāḥ kosalāḥ
kiṃ nāsti tvayi saty amātyavṛṣabhe yasmin karomi spṛhām || 84 || (4.21)
tathāpīdam astu bharatavākyam |
urvīm uddāmasasyāṃ janayatu visṛjanvāsavo vṛṣṭim iṣṭām
iṣṭais traiviṣṭapānāṃ vidadhatu vidhivatprīṇanaṃ vipramukhyāḥ |
ākalpāntaṃ ca bhūyat samupacitasukhaḥ saṃgamaḥ sajjanānāṃ
niḥśeṣā yāntu śāntiṃ piśunajanagiro durjayā vajralepāḥ || 84 || (4.22)
iti niṣkrāntāḥ sarve |
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Vasuṃdharā</s> enters.
(4.81) <s>Vasuṃdharā</s>: Victory, victory to the lord! Minister <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> humbly reports: this chief minister <s>Vasubhūti</s> of <s>Vikramabāhu</s> has been sent along with the chamberlain. The lord is pleased to see him at this very auspicious moment. And he says: 'I too, having attended to the remaining business, shall come presently.'
(4.82) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! Let the performance wait for now. The chief minister <s>Vasubhūti</s> has come from the maternal family. Let the noble lord see him first.
(4.83) King: As the queen says. (To the magician) Good sir, please rest now.
(4.84) The Magician: As the lord commands. But one more trick must absolutely be seen by the lord.
(4.85) King: Good sir, so be it. We shall see it.
(4.86) The magician exits.
(4.87) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>! Give him a reward.
(4.88) <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: As the queen commands. (She exits.)
(4.89) King: <s>Vasantaka</s>! Go to meet and escort <s>Vasubhūti</s> in.
(4.90) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: As the lord commands! (He exits.)
Then <s>Vasubhūti</s> and <s>Bābhravya</s> enter with <s>Vasantaka</s>.
(4.91) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Looking all around) Oh, the splendor of the palace gateway of the lord of <s>Vatsa</s>! For — [Verse 75:] Drawn aside by the victory-elephant, examining his beloved horses, / captivated by the sounds of music, standing a moment in the assemblies of kings, / instantly forgetting the grandeur of the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s> — oh, / in the corridors, with great curiosity, I have been made a rustic, just like a doorkeeper! //
(4.92) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Today, indeed, after so long I shall see my master — truly, from the excess of joy I am experiencing some altered state. Why? [Verse 76:] From timidity, it makes the trembling grow ever more, / with sheets of tears, it makes the blurred vision grow ever more, / with choking, it makes the faltering speech grow ever more — / my satisfaction today indeed renders assistance to old age! //
(4.93) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Going ahead) Let the minister come, come!
(4.94) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Seeing the jewel-necklace on the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>'s neck, aside) <s>Bābhravya</s>! I recognize it — this is the very jewel-necklace that was given by the king to the princess at the time of departure.
(4.95) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Minister! There is a resemblance. So shall I learn from <s>Vasantaka</s> the origin of this?
(4.96) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: <s>Bābhravya</s>! No, not so. In a great royal household, due to the abundance of jewels, the correspondence of ornaments is not uncommon.
(4.97) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Pointing toward the king) Here is the great king! So let the minister approach.
(4.98) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Approaching) May the great king be victorious!
(4.99) King: (Rising) Venerable sir! I salute you.
(4.100) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: May you prosper!
(4.101) King: A seat, a seat for the venerable one!
(4.102) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Bringing a seat) Here is a seat! So let the minister be seated.
(4.103) <s>Vasubhūti</s> sits down.
(4.104) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Minister! This is the queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, making her salutation.
(4.105) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Long-lived one! May you obtain a son worthy of <s>Vatsarāja</s>.
(4.106) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Sire! <s>Bābhravya</s> bows.
(4.107) King: (Placing his hand on his back) <s>Bābhravya</s>! Come, be seated here.
(4.108) <s>Bābhravya</s> sits down.
(4.109) King: Venerable <s>Vasubhūti</s>! Is the revered lord of <s>Siṃhala</s> well?
(4.110) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Looking upward and sighing) Sire! I do not know — what shall I, unfortunate one, report?
(4.111) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (With dejection, aside) Alas, alas! What will <s>Vasubhūti</s> say now?
(4.112) King: <s>Vasubhūti</s>! Speak! I am becoming anxious.
(4.113) <s>Bābhravya</s>: (Aside) Minister! What must be told even after long delay, let it be told now.
(4.114) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (With tears) It cannot be reported — yet I, unfortunate one, shall tell. Sire! That princess named <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, the daughter of the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s>, who was given to the lord — having been previously sought — upon hearing that the long-lived queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s> was burnt —
(4.115) King: (Aside) Queen! What is this falsehood that your maternal uncle's minister is telling?
(4.116) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! Even I do not know who is speaking falsely here.
(4.117) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Then what happened to her?
(4.118) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: And she, while being brought to your presence, sank into the ocean due to a shipwreck. (He stands weeping, face downward.)
(4.119) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (With tears) Alas, I am slain, unfortunate one! Alas, dear sister! Where are you? Give me an answer!
(4.120) King: Queen! Be consoled, be consoled! The course of destiny is hard to grasp. Are not these two — fallen and risen from a shipwreck — themselves your example? (He points to <s>Vasubhūti</s> and <s>Bābhravya</s>.)
(4.121) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! This is fitting. But whence come so many misfortunes for me?
(4.122) King: (Aside) <s>Bābhravya</s>! Tell me — what is this?
(4.123) (Commotion offstage.) [Verse 77:] Placing upon the golden pinnacles of mansions a beauty as if of heaps of flames, / revealing its utterly fierce heat through the withering of treetops in dense gardens, / making the pleasure-hill dark as a rain-cloud with masses of smoke, / tormenting the women-folk with burning — this fire has suddenly arisen in the inner chambers! // And further — [Verse 78:] This rumor of the queen's burning that once arose at <s>Lāvaṇaka</s> — / I think this fire has arisen as if to make that true. //
(4.124) King: (Rising in alarm) What! A fire in the inner chambers! Terrible! The queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s> is burnt! Alas, beloved <s>Vāsavadattā</s>!
(4.125) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Let the noble lord save himself! Save yourself!
(4.126) King: What! In my extreme agitation, I did not even notice the queen standing here! Queen! Be consoled, be consoled!
(4.127) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! I do not say this for my own sake! <s>Sāgarikā</s>, whom I, the cruel one, had confined here — she is in danger! So let the noble lord save her!
(4.128) King: What! <s>Sāgarikā</s> is in danger! Queen! I am going!
(4.129) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Sire! Why this recklessness without cause, like a moth?
(4.130) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Sire! <s>Vasubhūti</s> speaks rightly.
(4.131) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Seizing the king by his upper garment) Oh! Do not act rashly!
(4.132) King: (Pulling away his garment) Shame on you, fool! <s>Sāgarikā</s> is in danger — should I still cling to life? (Acting out being overwhelmed by smoke) [Verse 79:] Cease, cease, O fire! Release your trail of smoke! / Why do you raise high the circle of your flames? / I who was not burnt by the fire of separation from my beloved — / what can you do to me, with your blaze of cosmic dissolution? //
(4.133) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: What! Because of me, the cause of her suffering — the noble lord has thus resolved! Then I too shall follow him!
(4.134) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Walking around and going ahead) I too shall be a guide on the path!
(4.135) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: What! King <s>Vatsarāja</s> has entered the very flames! Then it is fitting for me too — having witnessed the princess's calamity — to offer myself as an oblation.
(4.136) <s>Bābhravya</s>: (With tears) Alas, great king! Why has the house of <s>Bharata</s> been placed in the balance of doubt without cause? But what use is lamentation? I too shall act as befits my devotion.
(All act out entering the fire.)
Then <s>Sāgarikā</s> enters, bound in fetters.
(4.137) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: Alas, alas! Oh! The fire, blazing on all sides, will today bring an end to my suffering!
(4.138) King: Ah! Here is <s>Sāgarikā</s>, with fire close upon her! I shall quickly attend to her!
(4.139) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: (Seeing the king, aside) What! The noble lord! Then, seeing this, hope for life has returned to me! (Aloud) Save me, save me, my lord!
(4.140) King: Timid one! Enough of fear! [Verse 80:] Bear this thick rising smoke for even a moment — / alas, shame — this garment of yours is burning, fallen from your breast! / Why do you stumble again and again — how, you are bound in fetters! Quickly, / I shall lead you from here, beloved — hold on to me! // (Embracing her neck, with eyes closed, acting out the touch) Oh! In an instant my torment has departed! Dear one! Be consoled, be consoled! [Verse 81:] Clearly, even the fire, though clinging, shall not burn you, / for this your touch, beloved, removes even the burning! // (Opening his eyes, looking around and releasing <s>Sāgarikā</s>) Oh, what great wonder! Where has that fire gone? The inner chambers are in the same state... (Seeing <s>Vāsavadattā</s>) ... What! This is the daughter of the king of <s>Avantī</s>!
(4.141) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Touching the king's body, with joy) Thank heavens! The noble lord's body is unharmed!
(4.142) King: This is <s>Bābhravya</s>...
(4.143) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Sire! Now I have been restored to life!
(4.144) King: ... this is <s>Vasubhūti</s>...
(4.145) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: May the great king be victorious!
(4.146) King: ... friend —
(4.147) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Victory, victory to you!
(4.148) King: (Reflecting, with doubt) [Verse 82:] Does the mind wander in a dream, or is this magic? //
(4.149) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Oh! Do not doubt! For that son of a slave-girl, the magician, said: 'One more trick of mine must absolutely be seen by the lord!'
(4.150) King: Queen! It was at your word that <s>Sāgarikā</s> was brought here.
(4.151) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Laughing) Noble lord! I know.
(4.152) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Examining <s>Sāgarikā</s>, aside) <s>Bābhravya</s>! She resembles the princess.
(4.153) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Minister! This is what I too have in mind.
(4.154) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Addressing the king) Sire! Whence is this maiden?
(4.155) King: The queen knows.
(4.156) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Queen! Whence then is this maiden?
(4.157) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Minister! She was placed in my hands by minister <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>, saying 'She has been obtained from a <s>sārikā</s> (mynah bird).' That is why she is called <s>Sāgarikā</s> (one from the ocean).
(4.158) King: (Aside) She was placed by <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>! How could he do anything without informing me?
(4.159) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: (Aside) <s>Bābhravya</s>! Given the close resemblance of the jewel-necklace on <s>Vasantaka</s>'s neck and her having been obtained from the sea, this is clearly the daughter of the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. (Approaching, aloud) Long-lived <s>Ratnāvalī</s>! You have come to such a state!
(4.160) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: (Seeing, with tears) What! Minister <s>Vasubhūti</s>!
(4.161) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Alas, I am slain, unfortunate one! (He falls to the ground.)
(4.162) <s>Sāgarikā</s>: (Falling upon <s>Vasubhūti</s>) Alas, father! Alas, mother! Where are you? Give me an answer!
(4.163) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (With alarm) Venerable <s>Kāñcukī</s>! This is my sister <s>Ratnāvalī</s>!
(4.164) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Queen! She is indeed.
(4.165) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Embracing <s>Ratnāvalī</s>) Sister! Be consoled, be consoled!
(4.166) King: What! She is the daughter of the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Vikramabāhu</s>, who is of illustrious lineage!
(4.167) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Seeing <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, aside) I said it from the very first — such an ornament is surely not the possession of a common person!
(4.168) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (With tears, extending her arms) Oh come! Dear sister! At least now, show me the affection of kinship!
(4.169) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Long-lived one! Be consoled, be consoled! Is not this your elder sister grieving? So embrace her!
(4.170) <s>Ratnāvalī</s>: (Recovering, glancing sideways at the king, aside) How unfortunate I am before the queen! I cannot show my face! (She stands with face downcast.)
(4.171) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: (Aside) Noble lord! I am ashamed of my own cruelty. So remove her bonds.
(4.172) King: (With satisfaction) As the queen says. (He frees <s>Sāgarikā</s>.)
(4.173) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! Minister <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> has treated me harshly for so long, since even knowing [the truth], he did not inform me.
Then <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> enters.
(4.174) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: [Verse 83:] At my word, the queen accepted the separation from her lord, as agreed; / she was kept in suffering by me for the sake of the lord's union with a consort; / this lordship over the earth that the master has gained will bring her joy — / yet truly, I cannot show my face out of shame. // But then, what can one do? Such is the vow of devotion to the master — acting without regard even for those who are most worthy of respect. (Looking) Here is the lord. Let me approach. (Approaching) Victory, victory to the lord! Sire! May I be forgiven for what I have done without informing you.
(4.175) King: <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>! What was done without informing me?
(4.176) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: Let the lord take a seat. I shall report everything.
(All sit down.)
(4.177) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: Sire! Listen. This daughter of the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s> — a <s>siddha</s> (perfected ascetic) prophesied regarding her: 'Whoever takes her hand in marriage shall become a universal sovereign.' Then, by faith in that [prophecy], though repeatedly sought by us on behalf of the master, the lord of <s>Siṃhala</s>, wishing to avoid distressing queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, did not give her.
(4.178) King: Then what?
(4.179) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: Then, having spread the report that the queen was burnt at <s>Lāvaṇaka</s>, <s>Bābhravya</s> was dispatched to him.
(4.180) King: <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>! From this point on I have already heard. But why was she placed in the queen's hands, upon what consideration?
(4.181) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Even what was not told, one knows — that once placed in the inner chambers, she would easily come within your sight through a friend of yours!
(4.182) King: <s>Vasantaka</s> has grasped your intent!
(4.183) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: As the lord commands.
(4.184) King: The magician episode too, I think, was your contrivance.
(4.185) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: Otherwise, how could the lord see her when she was confined in the inner chambers? And how could <s>Vasubhūti</s> recognize her without seeing her? (Laughing) And now that the sister has been recognized, as to what should be done — the queen is the authority in that matter.
(4.186) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! Why do you not say plainly: 'Accept <s>Ratnāvalī</s> from me'?
(4.187) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Lady! You have understood the minister's intent well!
(4.188) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Come, <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, come! Let at least this much befit my sister. (Adorning <s>Ratnāvalī</s> with her own ornaments, taking her hand, and approaching the king) Noble lord! Accept this <s>Ratnāvalī</s>!
(4.189) King: (With joy, extending his hands) Who would not esteem the queen's grace?
(4.190) <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: Noble lord! Her family is far away. So treat her in such a way that she does not miss her kinfolk. (She presents her.)
(4.191) King: As the queen commands.
(4.192) <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Dancing with joy) Hurrah! Victory, victory to you! The earth is now in the hands of our dear friend!
(4.193) <s>Vasubhūti</s>: Queen! Rightly do you bear the title of queen.
(4.194) <s>Bābhravya</s>: Now my toil has borne fruit.
(4.195) <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>: Sire! What further service of joy may I render?
(4.196) King: What further joy could there be? For — [Verse 84:] <s>Vikramabāhu</s> has been brought to equality with myself, this <s>Sāgarikā</s> is obtained — / the beloved, the sole cause of gaining the earth with its oceans — / the queen is pleased by the gain of a sister, the <s>Kosalas</s> are conquered — / is there anything, O bull among ministers, in which I feel longing when you exist? // Yet let there be this <s>Bharatavākya</s> (benedictory verse): [Verse 85:] May <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), releasing wished-for rain, make the earth abound with crops; / may the foremost among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> duly perform the propitiation of the gods with desired offerings; / and may the joyful union of good people, rich in happiness, last until the end of time; / may the words of slanderers — invincible, hard as diamond-cement — all reach peace! //
(All exit.)

body.text: iti caturtho 'ṅkaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth act.
